docs.title: Irrigated Cropland Mapping with Geospatial Foundation Models
docs.text:
Evaluating geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) for irrigated cropland mapping in North Africa and their transferability to data-scarce regions

Irrigated agriculture covers about a fifth of the world's cropland but produces around 40% of its food and accounts for most freshwater withdrawals. Knowing where and how much land is irrigated is therefore essential for water management and food security, especially in water-stressed regions such as North Africa. Yet most countries lack accurate, regularly updated irrigation maps, and existing global products are coarse or static. Geospatial foundation models, large models pretrained on vast archives of satellite imagery, promise accurate maps from few labels and better transfer to new regions. This research evaluates that promise for irrigated cropland mapping, using Morocco as a case study and Utah (USA) as a second, independent study area. It asks how accurately these models separate irrigated from rainfed cropland compared with conventional satellite-based methods, how much adapting them to the task helps, how consistent their maps are from year to year, and how well a model trained in Morocco transfers to a region with little ground truth.

docs.title: D1. Spatial folds instead of a 70/30 split
docs.text:
• Proposal (§4.1): stratified 70 / 30 split, validation subset from the training data. (§4.2.4 already asks for spatial cross-validation.)
  • Now: parcels grouped into 20 km blocks, blocks into 5 folds with equal class balance; every parcel tested once by a model that never saw its block.
  • Why: with a random split, 79% of test parcels lie within 250 m of a training parcel (about 2% with 20 km blocks). Random splits overstate accuracy for mapping new areas (Roberts et al. 2017; Ploton et al. 2020).
  • Where: dataset §5, protocol §2.

docs.title: D2. Two agricultural years (per-parcel season)
docs.text:
• Proposal (§4.1): the 2024 annual image stack.
  • Now: each parcel gets the 12 months (1 Sep – 31 Aug) of the season in which it was surveyed: 2023/24 or 2024/25. Both seasons in one dataset, months aligned (month 1 = September).
  • Why: the survey ran Dec 2023 – Jan 2025; using only 2024 would mix seasons, and dropping 2024/25 would lose 42% of the rainfed parcels. The agricultural year covers the winter rainfed cycle and the summer, when only irrigated fields stay green.
  • Consequence: region and year are partly confounded (Gharb and Tadla only 2023/24, Souss only 2024/25).
  • Where: dataset §6.2.

docs.title: D3. Validation: PASTIS rotation instead of nested CV
docs.text:
• Before (E01): nested spatial CV, settings by inner CV on the 4 training folds, refit on 4.
  • Now: per round 3 folds train, the next fold chooses the settings (or stops training), 1 fold tests, as in PASTIS (Garnot & Landrieu 2021).
  • Why: one design for classical classifiers and neural networks (L-TAE, fine-tuning), which need a separate validation fold for early stopping. It is the standard design of the PASTIS crop-mapping benchmark.
  • Where: protocol §2; E01 is kept as the sensitivity check.

docs.title: D4. One shared tile store for every input
docs.text:
• Proposal: annual Sentinel-1/2 composites via STAC and xarray.
  • Now: Google Earth Engine builds non-overlapping 128 × 128 px tiles (1.28 km) with 12 monthly composites × 19 bands; the baseline features and the foundation-model chips are all cut from these tiles.
  • Why: STAC processing was too slow for the full set; with one store every input sees identical pixels, compositing and masks, and chips no longer overlap across folds.
  • Where: dataset §6–7.

docs.title: D5. Frozen encoder + classical classifiers
docs.text:
Parcel-wise (archived); superseded by D16

In the pixel-wise experiments the frozen encoder is followed by L-TAE and a UPerNet head (E04), and RQ2 compares frozen, LoRA, full fine-tuning and training from scratch (E05).

  • Proposal (§4.2.1): frozen encoder, train a decoder and classification head.
  • Now: the task is per parcel, so the frozen encoder gives one embedding per parcel and the "head" is a classifier (linear probe and three others). Fine-tuning (RQ2) follows.
  • Why: tests what the pretrained representation already contains, at equal cost for every model; the linear probe is the standard test of frozen features.

docs.title: D6. Four classifiers instead of one Random Forest
docs.text:
Parcel-wise (archived)

The pixel-wise baselines are the random forest and gradient boosting (E01) and TempCNN (E02).

  • Proposal: Random Forest baseline.
  • Now: logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting and SVM on every input (RF stays the headline).
  • Why: a classifier that suits hand-built features (RF) may not suit dense embeddings (E01: RF is the weakest classifier on embeddings). Reporting all four keeps the comparison from depending on one choice.
  • Update (12 Nov 2026): from E02 on, three classifiers: logistic regression (linear probe), random forest (standard remote-sensing classifier, the proposal's baseline) and SVM (strongest in E01), plus a trainable MLP head (E03, E04). Gradient boosting is dropped: in E01 it was never the best classifier and always within the confidence interval of SVM. Plan: parcel-wise experiment plan.

docs.title: D7. Macro-F1 as the headline metric
docs.text:
• Proposal (§4.2.4): OA, precision, recall, F1; best model by mean F1 over the five folds, SD as consistency.
  • Now: macro-F1 of all out-of-fold predictions with a 95% block-bootstrap CI as headline; per-fold mean ± SD is reported too, as the proposal asked.
  • Why: with 86% irrigated parcels, overall accuracy and irrigated F1 are high for any model; macro-F1 weights the rainfed class equally. Paired bootstrap differences say whether a gap is real.

docs.title: D8. Two temporal aggregation pipelines
docs.text:
Parcel-wise (archived)

In the pixel-wise experiments the image GeoFMs use L-TAE over the months at every patch position (E04).

  • Proposal: not specified.
  • Now: PCA pipeline (concat 12 months → PCA 128) in E01 / E02; L-TAE pipeline in E04.
  • Why: PANGAEA (Marsocci et al. 2024) found L-TAE better than linear mapping for single-date encoders; testing both shows whether the conclusion depends on how the months are combined.
  • Where: protocol §5.

docs.title: D9. Cloud Score+ instead of QA60
docs.text:
• Now: Sentinel-2 pixels kept when Cloud Score+ cs_cdf ≥ 0.60; scenes with up to 60% cloud admitted.
  • Why: the QA60 band misses thin cloud and shadow; Cloud Score+ is the recommended mask in Earth Engine (Pasquarella et al. 2023).

docs.title: D10. Transfer region under review
docs.text:
• Proposal (§3.2): zero-shot transfer to Tunisia, validated on 54 GMIA-NEXT points (44 irrigated, 10 rainfed).
  • Now: Morocco first. As an alternative, US state datasets with both irrigated and dryland fields (eastern Washington WSDA, Utah WRLU 2017–2025) would allow a spatial and a multi-year test with the same pipeline.
  • Why: 10 rainfed points are too few to measure a rainfed F1; the US data needs a check of its labels (see the progress log, 4–5 Nov 2026).
  • Decided (12 Nov 2026): Utah (WRLU) as the second region. Explicit rainfed class ("Dry Crop"), 13,000–17,000 rainfed crop fields per year, every year 2017–2025 with one method, one UTM zone. Eastern Washington was the fallback: most of its dryland-wheat fields come from the NASS Cropland Data Layer (irrigation not observed).
  • Superseded the same day by D13: Utah is not a transfer target but an independent second study area.

docs.title: D11. Two kinds of head: parcel benchmark and mapping model
docs.text:
Superseded by D16 (18 Nov 2026)

Every model now classifies pixels, so the parcel benchmark and the separate mapping model became one pixel-wise set-up. "E05" below is the archived PSE-TAE experiment, not the current E05.

  • Proposal (§4.2.1, §4.3): frozen encoder with a decoder / head; annual irrigated maps 2021–2025 for Morocco.
  • Problem: the RQ1 pipeline pools the embeddings over the parcel polygon. Annual maps of Morocco (or of a transfer region) have no polygons, and the GeoFM patches (80 m Clay, 160 m the others) are too coarse for parcels of 0.83 ha (median, about 90 m across).
  • Now:
  • RQ1 benchmark (unchanged): frozen encoder → parcel embedding → LogReg (linear probe), RF, HGB, SVM; plus L-TAE + MLP head (E04). Classical heads on frozen embeddings are common practice (Presto; WorldCereal; AlphaEarth irrigated mapping, Yang et al. 2026) and the head matters little in recent comparisons (Mughees et al. 2026).
  • Mapping models (RQ2–RQ4): frozen GeoFM + UPerNet segmentation head trained on the label pixels of the tiles (as in PANGAEA and Prithvi-EO-2.0), then LoRA with the same head (RQ2). Classical baseline: RF on the S1/S2 features of each pixel.
  • Neural baselines from scratch: TempCNN (per-pixel time series; Pelletier et al. 2019) and U-TAE (tiles; Garnot & Landrieu 2021). Both produce 10 m maps. PSE-TAE needs parcel polygons and stays a parcel-level extra (E05).
  • Same scoring: pixel predictions are aggregated per parcel (mean probability) and scored with the same folds, parcels and bootstrap as RQ1, so every number stays comparable.
  • Why: the research must end in wall-to-wall annual maps; a 1D-CNN beat RF for irrigated mapping (Bazzi et al. 2019) and TempCNN-type models transferred better across regions than GeoFM embeddings (Tong & Wang 2025), so a neural baseline is needed next to the classical one.
  • Where: literature notes.

docs.title: D12. AgriFM with its pretrained 4-px patch embedding
docs.text:
• Before: 06d_embed_agrifm.py built the Sentinel-2 encoder with the patch size of the repository's fine-tuning configuration (configs/cropland_mapping.py: 4 time steps × 2 × 2 px, output stride 16 px) and loaded AgriFM.pth through mmengine. No weight was loaded: the checkpoint names carry the prefix encoder., and the pretrained patch embedding (S2_patch_emd, kernel 128 × 10 × 4 × 4 × 4) does not fit a 2 × 2 px patch. mmengine only warns about mismatched names and still reports success, so all AgriFM embeddings produced up to 6 Nov 2026 (local and on the cluster, including E01) came from a randomly initialised encoder.
  • Now: patch size 4 × 4 × 4 (the size of the pretrained patch embedding), output stride 32 px (320 m; 2 × 2 cells per 64-px chip). The weights are mapped by name in the script and every encoder tensor must load; otherwise the script stops. On the cluster 349 of 349 encoder tensors load.
  • Why: the frozen-encoder comparison (D5) must use each encoder as pretrained. In the fine-tuning set-up of the repository the 2 × 2 px patch embedding is trained anew; with a frozen encoder it would stay random. The alternative, resizing the 4 × 4 px kernel to 2 × 2 px, keeps a finer grid but replaces the pretrained first layer by an approximation.
  • Consequence: AgriFM has the coarsest grid of the four models (320 m against 80–160 m), which matters for small parcels; the patch-share weighting is unchanged. Earlier AgriFM results are void and are re-run.
  • Where: parcelwise_run/06d_embed_agrifm.py, Foundation models · inputs.

docs.title: D13. Utah as a second independent study area
docs.text:
• Proposal (§3.2, RQ3, RQ4): RQ4 applies the Morocco-trained model zero-shot to a transfer region (Tunisia, 54 GMIA-NEXT points); RQ3 tests temporal consistency within Morocco.
  • Now:
    • Utah is an independent second study area. It is trained and tested on its own data (WRLU labels), with the same pipeline, foundation models, classifiers and evaluation as Morocco; the two regions are reported side by side. There is no Morocco → Utah transfer.
    • Temporal test in Utah: train on WRLU 2024 (2023/24), test on WRLU 2021 (2020/21) on the folds held out in training (same fields in both years, paired comparison). See Utah training data, section 10.
    • Years: WRLU 2024 (training) and 2021 (test). Between them 36% of the crops change but only 0.07% of the fields change class; 2025 repeats 94% of the 2024 crops and is not an independent year; 2019 shows a sudden jump in class changes (1.35%) that may be a revision of the mapping.
  • Why:
    • A Morocco → Utah transfer mixes a change of region, climate, crop calendar (Utah is 2–3 months later), label source and field size; a low score would not say which of these failed. Two independent studies show whether the conclusions on the foundation models hold in a second region.
    • Morocco cannot offer a clean temporal test (the surveyed regions differ between the two years); in Utah the same places are mapped every year.
    • Tunisia has 10 rainfed reference points, too few for a rainfed F1 (D10).
  • Consequence: RQ4 changes from "spatial transferability of the Morocco model" to "do the results hold in a second region"; RQ3 is answered in Utah. To be agreed with the supervisors.
  • Where: Utah training data, pixelwise_run/01_prepare_labels_Utah.py.

docs.title: D14. Sentinel-2 only for every input
docs.text:
• Proposal: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series.
  • Before: the baseline used Sentinel-2 + Sentinel-1 features (one orbit), TerraMind received Sentinel-2 + Sentinel-1, the other three GeoFMs Sentinel-2 only.
  • Now: every input of the model comparison uses Sentinel-2 only: the four GeoFMs (TerraMind with MODALITIES = ["S2L2A"]), the feature baseline (S1S2_VARIABLES = "s2") and PSE-TAE (BANDS = "s2"). No model is given an input it was not pretrained on, and no fusion of embeddings with radar features is designed for the optical-only models.
  • Why:
    • Every model sees the same optical data, so a difference comes from the representation and the head, not from one model having radar.
    • Morocco and Utah are treated alike.
    • Sentinel-1 coverage of Utah changed between the years: after Sentinel-1B failed (December 2021) only Sentinel-1A covered the area in 2023/24 (only the descending orbit was usable), while the 2020/21 test year had both satellites. With radar, the 2024 → 2021 temporal test (D13) would partly measure a change in radar coverage.
  • Consequence: the multimodal pretraining of TerraMind is not used in the main comparison. An optional ablation in Morocco (both orbits available) adds Sentinel-1 to TerraMind (terramind-s1s2) and to the baseline (S1S2_VARIABLES = "all", PSE-TAE morocco_s2s1). E01 (done before this decision) used Sentinel-1 in the baseline and in TerraMind and is kept as it is.
  • Where: Foundation models · Configuration, Models pipeline.

docs.title: D15. AgriFM normalised with the statistics of the region's chips
docs.text:
• Before: AgriFM inputs were normalised with the statistics of the repository's fine-tuning example (configs/cropland_mapping.py).
  • Problem: neither the AgriFM paper (Li et al. 2025) nor the repository documents the normalisation of the pretraining data. The config statistics (blue 4,179 ± 4,042) describe raw, partly cloudy time series; the cloud-masked monthly composites of this study have blue 714 ± 344 (Morocco). With the config statistics the visible and NIR bands use only 8–30% of the expected spread and sit about 0.8 SD below zero, so the frozen encoder sees an almost constant input in these bands.
  • Now: per-band mean and standard deviation of the region's own chips (NORM = "data" in 06d_embed_agrifm.py): all valid pixels of 20 evenly spaced chip files, every 4th pixel; computed from imagery only (no labels), saved to agrifm_norm_stats_<tag>.json and reused. For the Utah temporal test the 2023/24 statistics are reused for 2020/21 (NORM_STATS_FILE), so both years are scaled identically.
  • Why: standardising each band to zero mean and unit variance is what a z-score normalisation with the pretraining statistics does on the pretraining data; when those statistics are unknown, the data's own statistics are the closest equivalent.
  • Sensitivity: the config statistics are kept as a second embedding (NORM = "config", agrifm-cfgnorm_*.npz; the Morocco file made on 6 Nov 2026 is this version).
  • Where: Foundation models · AgriFM, parcelwise_run/06d_embed_agrifm.py.

docs.title: D16. Pixel-wise classification for continuous maps
docs.text:
• Before: the RQ1 experiments (E01–E05) classified parcels: the embeddings or Sentinel-2 features of a parcel were averaged inside its outline and classified as one sample.
  • Problem: the final product is an annual, continuous (wall-to-wall) map. A parcel-wise model needs a parcel outline for every field it classifies, and outlines exist only for the surveyed parcels.
  • Now: every 10 m pixel is classified on its own. Training and test samples are the labelled pixels of the surveyed parcels (pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py); a pixel takes its parcel's label and fold, so no parcel is split between training and test. The pixel-wise results are not compared with the archived parcel-wise E01–E05.
  • Kept: labels, spatial folds (20 km blocks, 5 folds, PASTIS rotation), the tile store and its compositing, Sentinel-2 only (D14), metrics and statistics.
  • Archive: E01–E05 with their pages, results and scripts are kept unchanged in the Archive; they remain the RQ1 evidence at parcel level.
  • Where: Pixel samples, pixel-wise experiment plan.

docs.title: D17. Cropland mask from four products and a "not cropland" class
docs.text:
Experiments changed by D19 (20 Nov 2026)

The experiments no longer use the mask or the not-cropland class (two classes on the surveyed parcels). The mask below stays the candidate for the mapping phase, where it will be compared with single products.

  • Before: not specified; WorldCover 2021 was used only to check the survey parcels.
  • Now: the mapped area of each agricultural year is the union of 4 cropland products (ESA WorldCover 2021, Esri LULC of the year, GCEP30, GLAD 2019): a pixel is cropland if any product calls it cropland; WorldCover built-up, snow and water are removed. The models have a third class, not cropland, trained on pixels that no product calls cropland, so they can remove the union's false cropland. The mask is applied to the map output, never to the model inputs; labelled parcels outside the mask stay in training and are only flagged.
  • Why: each product alone misses surveyed cropland (WorldCover 78% of the irrigated test parcels, GCEP30 99%, union 100%); combining products is established practice (Meier et al. 2018; Xie et al. 2021; Teluguntla et al. 2023), and IrrMapper handled non-cropland as extra classes instead of an external mask (Ketchum et al. 2020). A mask that uses no field labels has the same quality in labelled and unlabelled areas.
  • Reporting: accuracy of the classifier on labelled pixels; omission of the mask on the surveyed parcels (mask_check.csv); accuracy of the final map from an independent sample over the map, including non-cropland.
  • Where: Cropland extent and mask, cropland_extent/make_cropland_mask.py.

docs.title: D18. Wall-to-wall composites from STAC for the maps
docs.text:
• Proposal: annual stacks via STAC and xarray.
  • Before: one Google Earth Engine tile store (D4), built around the surveyed parcels; too slow for every cropland tile of Morocco (48 MB request limit, about 40 h per year on one stream).
  • Now: monthly Sentinel-2 composites of every tile with ≥ 1% cropland are downloaded from a public STAC catalogue (Earth Search, sentinel-2-c1-l2a; SCL cloud mask; offset of processing baseline ≥ 04.00 removed), per 10.24 km block of 8 × 8 tiles, as many parallel jobs on the cluster. The STAC approach is independent of the Earth Engine tiles: its models are trained, evaluated and mapped on STAC tiles only.
  • Status (20 Nov 2026): Utah 2023/24 17,278 of 18,472 tiles (the rest after a fix); Morocco on hold.
  • Where: s2_download/, experiment plan §3.

docs.title: D19. Two-class experiments; cropland extent in the mapping phase
docs.text:
• Before (D17): three classes in the experiments: irrigated, rainfed and "not cropland", the last one trained on pixels that none of the cropland products calls cropland.
  • Problem: the not-cropland labels come from the products, not from the field (weak labels, and only the easy cases with 0 votes); they mix the question "where is cropland?" into the comparison of models, and part of a model's score depended on how often it confused surveyed fields with that weak class.
  • Now: the experiments compare models only on what has ground truth: the pixels of the surveyed parcels, all of them cropland, in two classes, irrigated and rainfed (headline: macro-F1 of the two). No cropland mask is used in labels, samples or experiments. Where cropland is, and how non-cropland is handled on the maps, is decided in the mapping phase: candidate masks (the union of products of make_cropland_mask.py, Dynamic World alone (download_dynamic_world.py), others) are compared on the omission of surveyed irrigated and rainfed parcels and on commission, and the maps are assessed with an independent sample.
  • Consequences: all pixel-wise experiments (E01–E05) are run again in two classes, Morocco first, then Utah; the earlier 3-class results were removed. Pixel samples: pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py (04_pixel_samples/).
  • Where: Experiment plan, Pixel samples, Cropland extent and mask.

docs.title: Foundation models
docs.text: Six geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) are evaluated in this study: four image models and two pixel time-series models. This page summarises their design and pretraining, specifies how each model is applied in the pixel-wise experiments (Morocco first, then Utah), and lists the primary sources. Other pages refer to this page rather than repeating its content.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: The models were selected according to three criteria: (i) pretrained weights are openly available and can be fine-tuned; (ii) the models accept multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and/or Sentinel-2 input; and (iii) together they represent the principal GeoFM families, namely masked-autoencoder Vision Transformers (Prithvi-EO-2.0, Clay), a multimodal generative model (TerraMind), an agriculture-specific spatio-temporal model (AgriFM) and two models that encode the time series of a single pixel (Presto, TESSERA). The four image models encode patches of 80–320 m; the two pixel models work at the 10 m resolution of the maps, which matches the pixel-wise classification of the study (D16).

docs.title: Configuration in this study
docs.text:
Every model classifies every 10 m pixel (D16). The encoders see whole 128 × 128 px tiles (1.28 km) of 12 monthly Sentinel-2 composites of the agricultural year, with the bands, band order, normalisation and weights of their own pretraining. Every input uses Sentinel-2 only (D14): every model sees the same optical data, and Sentinel-1 coverage of Utah changed between the years. All six encoders are loaded by pixelwise_run/encoders.py.

flowchart LR A["128 px tile<br/>12 months, Sentinel-2"] --> B["Encoder<br/>(frozen, fine-tuned<br/>or from scratch)"] B --> C["L-TAE over the months<br/>(image models)"] C --> D["Feature pyramid<br/>+ UPerNet head"] D --> E["irrigated / rainfed<br/>per 10 m pixel"]

docs.text:

The head (L-TAE where used, feature pyramid and UPerNet; 2.4–3.2 M weights with the image models) is the same for every model; its design and the training settings are on the E04 page.

docs.title: Frozen, fine-tuned or trained from scratch
docs.text:
How much of the encoder is trained differs between the experiments (RQ2 · Fine-tuning explains the strategies):

Experiment Models Encoder Trained E04 (RQ1) all six frozen: pretrained weights, no gradient updates, evaluation mode head only (2.4–3.2 M weights with the image models) E05 (RQ2) Prithvi-EO-2.0, Morocco first frozen, LoRA (low-rank adapters, rank 16, on the attention and MLP layers), fully fine-tuned (every weight, encoder learning rate 10⁻⁵, head 10⁻⁴) or from scratch (same network from random weights); 10, 25, 50 or 100% of the training parcels head only (frozen), 5.5 M adapters + head (LoRA), or all ≈ 306 M weights

docs.title: Earlier parcel-wise benchmark (archived)
docs.text:
The first benchmark (archive) classified whole parcels in Morocco with the four image models, all frozen. Each model received a 64 × 64 px chip (640 m) centred on the parcel, and the parcel embedding was the mean of the patch tokens covering the parcel, weighted by the fraction of each patch inside the parcel (Models pipeline §5). These embeddings cannot give wall-to-wall maps, which is why the study moved to the pixel-wise set-up (D16).

Input Chips Bands Patch Temporal handling Output per parcel Script S2 baseline parcel features (inner pixels) 12 S2 bands, NDVI, NDWI, EVI parcel median 12 months concatenated 180 features 03 Clay v1.5 p8 10 S2 bands 8 px (80 m) one month per forward pass 12 × 1024 02a Prithvi-EO-2.0 p16 6 S2 bands (HLS set) 16 px (160 m) four months per pass, three passes 12 × 1024 02b TerraMind p16 12 S2 bands 16 px (160 m) one month per forward pass 12 × 768 02c AgriFM p16 10 S2 bands 4 px pretrained patch embedding; output stride 32 px (320 m) full 12-month stack in one pass 1 × 1024 02d

An optional ablation of that benchmark (Morocco only) added Sentinel-1 where a model was pretrained on it: TerraMind with Sentinel-1 (MODALITIES = ["S2L2A", "S1GRD"] in script 02c, written as terramind-s1s2_agyear_tiles.npz) and the baseline with radar features (S1S2_VARIABLES = "all" in script 03).

docs.title: Clay v1.5
docs.text: Clay encodes each band together with its central wavelength, which allows a single model to process imagery from different sensors. Ten Sentinel-2 bands (B2–B8A, B11, B12) are standardised with the statistics of Clay's metadata.yaml. Additional inputs are the pixel size (10 m), the acquisition date (week of year, sine/cosine encoded; monthly composites are dated mid-month) and the location (latitude and longitude, sine/cosine encoded). The model processes one date per forward pass, so the twelve months are embedded independently. With 8 px patches, a 128 px tile yields a 16 × 16 token grid (8 × 8 for the 64 px chips of the archived parcel benchmark).

docs.title: Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL
docs.text: Prithvi-EO-2.0 is pretrained on HLS time series and encodes acquisition date and location explicitly. The six HLS bands (Blue, Green, Red, Narrow NIR, SWIR 1, SWIR 2; Sentinel-2 B2, B3, B4, B8A, B11, B12) are standardised with the model's pretraining statistics. Following the pretraining configuration, four frames are processed per pass (September–December, January–April, May–August); each frame retains its own tokens, giving one vector per month. The model is loaded through TerraTorch (prithvi_eo_v2_300_tl). Limitation: pretraining used 30 m HLS data, whereas 10 m Sentinel-2 is used here; the resulting 160 m patch is closer to typical parcel size than the 480 m patch at native resolution.

docs.title: TerraMind-1.0-base
docs.text: TerraMind is trained to generate any of nine modalities from any other and therefore learns a joint representation of optical, radar and auxiliary data. The pixel-wise experiments supply only S2L2A (B1–B12), standardised with TerraMind's pretraining statistics (D14). The Sentinel-1 ablation of the archived parcel benchmark also supplied S1GRD (VV, VH in dB) and averaged the tokens of the two modalities (merge_method = "mean"). One date is processed per pass; 16 px patches give an 8 × 8 token grid on a 128 px tile (4 × 4 on a 64 px chip).

docs.title: AgriFM
docs.text:
AgriFM is designed for crop mapping and models the temporal dimension within the network. The full 12-month stack of ten Sentinel-2 bands is processed in a single pass. Input tokens span four time steps and 4 × 4 px (the pretrained patch embedding); the final feature map has a stride of 32 px (D12). Because time is compressed inside the network, there is one set of features per season: in the pixel-wise experiments its four-level feature pyramid goes directly to the UPerNet head; the archived parcel benchmark pooled it to one vector per parcel. Only the encoder is used, through the mmengine registries of the cloned repository.

Normalisation (D15). Neither the AgriFM paper nor the repository documents the normalisation of the pretraining data; the only published statistics belong to the repository's fine-tuning example (configs/cropland_mapping.py, blue 4,179 ± 4,042). The cloud-masked composites of this study are on a different scale (Morocco blue 714 ± 344), so with the config statistics the visible and NIR bands would use only 8–30% of the expected spread. AgriFM is therefore normalised per band with the mean and standard deviation of the region's own chips (NORM = "data"; statistics saved to agrifm_norm_stats_<tag>.json), the usual choice when the pretraining statistics are unknown. The config statistics are kept as a sensitivity run (NORM = "config", file agrifm-cfgnorm_*.npz).

docs.title: Presto
docs.text: Presto tokenises a pixel's time series by channel group and month (Sentinel-1, three Sentinel-2 groups, NIR, SWIR, ERA5, SRTM, NDVI, Dynamic World) and adds the month and the location. Sentinel-2 only (D14): the Sentinel-1, ERA5, SRTM and Dynamic World tokens are masked, which the model supports (masked tokens are removed). Sentinel-2 is divided by 10,000 as in pretraining. Presto requires the same tokens to be masked for all pixels of a batch, so months without a clear observation are filled by linear interpolation in time. The embedding is the normalised mean of the encoder tokens (128-d).

docs.title: TESSERA v2
docs.text: TESSERA encodes the Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 observations of a pixel as unordered sets dated by their day of year and pools them with attention into a 128-d embedding (Matryoshka-ordered: the first 16, 32 or 64 dimensions are usable on their own). The Medium student is used, as recommended by the authors. TESSERA was trained on single acquisitions; here each observation is a monthly composite dated the 15th of its month, and only clear months are used, padded or subsampled to the observation-count bin of the reference code (8 or 16). Sentinel-2 only: the Sentinel-1 branch receives one empty observation, as the reference code does without Sentinel-1.

All weights are stored in checkpoints/<model>/ (excluded from version control) and are downloaded automatically on the first use (pixelwise_run/encoders.py).

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Research proposal

Research proposal (PDF)

docs.title: Why irrigated cropland matters
docs.text:
Irrigated agriculture covers only about 20% of the world's cultivated land, yet it produces around 40% of global food and accounts for about 70% of all freshwater withdrawals (Wu et al., 2023). With population growth, climate change and increasing water scarcity, reliable information on where irrigation takes place, and how it changes from year to year, is essential for water management, agricultural planning and the Sustainable Development Goals on food (SDG 2) and water (SDG 6).

Morocco is a demanding and relevant case. Agriculture provides about 14% of its GDP, 39% of national employment and 74% of rural employment, and the country has developed more than two million hectares of irrigated land across seven large schemes. At the same time it is among the most water-stressed countries in the world: agriculture uses over 80% of the available water, while rainfall has fallen by about 30% over three decades. National programmes (the Green Morocco Plan 2008–2020 and the Green Generation strategy 2020–2030) expanded drip irrigation from 160,000 ha in 2008 to 585,000 ha in 2019 (Guemouria et al., 2023). Tracking whether this expansion meets its goals, and where water use is most intensive, requires precise and up-to-date irrigated cropland maps.

Much of the rest of North Africa lacks the dense, field-verified irrigation data that exists for Morocco. Methods that can be trained where labels are rich and transferred to agro-climatically similar, data-scarce regions would be a significant step for agricultural monitoring across the region.

docs.title: State of the art
docs.text:
Approach Examples Limitation Global irrigation products GMIA (Siebert et al., 2005; ~9 km), GIAM (Thenkabail et al., 2009) far too coarse for fields of a few hectares 30 m global maps LGRIP30 (Teluguntla et al., 2023; 86.5% overall accuracy), GMIE (Wu et al., 2023) static snapshots or decade-maximum extents, no annual series; locally calibrated thresholds Machine learning on Sentinel-1/2 time series current state of the art for field-scale irrigation mapping depends on hand-built spectral and temporal features; degrades when applied to new regions; hard to combine sensors (Yang et al., 2026)

Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) offer a different route. They are large neural networks pretrained with self-supervised learning on vast unlabelled satellite archives. They learn rich spatio-temporal representations directly from the imagery, without hand-built features, can be adapted to a task with few labels, and may transfer across regions and sensors (Tseng et al., 2023; Szwarcman et al., 2024). Adaptation ranges from a frozen encoder with a light classification head, through parameter-efficient fine-tuning such as LoRA, to full fine-tuning.

docs.title: Research gap
docs.text:
1. No annual irrigated cropland maps exist for Morocco or other North African countries. Global products give static extents, not the year-by-year maps needed to monitor irrigation expansion and evaluate policy. This needs a model that is accurate and consistent from one year to the next.
  2. No geospatial foundation model has been evaluated for irrigated cropland mapping, and none in Africa's diverse agro-hydrological landscapes, from semi-arid to sub-humid climates and from flood to drip and pivot irrigation.
  3. It is unknown which foundation model suits the task best, how much fine-tuning adds to a frozen encoder, and whether a model trained in one region still works in a data-scarce region nearby.

docs.title: Objectives and research questions
docs.text:
Main objective: to compare the performance and transferability of geospatial foundation models for irrigated cropland mapping.

Objective Research question 1 · Compare models and adaptation strategies in Morocco RQ1 What classification accuracy does each foundation model achieve for irrigated cropland mapping across Morocco's agricultural regions, and how does it compare with a conventional Sentinel-based classifier? RQ2 To what extent does fine-tuning (LoRA or full fine-tuning) improve on a frozen encoder, compared with training from scratch? 2 · Evaluate temporal and spatial transferability of the best model RQ3 How temporally consistent is the best model across years, and does the annual map series for Morocco (2021–2025) reflect the irrigation trends in national statistics? RQ4 When the Morocco-trained model is applied without retraining to another region, how much does accuracy degrade, and do its annual maps stay consistent? 3 · Optional extension: multi-model fusion RQ5 Does fusing the embeddings of several foundation models improve on the best single model?

Research questions as proposed

The questions above follow the research proposal; RQ2 is worded as it is now tested. Changes to the design since the proposal are recorded in Decisions, in particular D13 (Utah as an independent second study area instead of a zero-shot transfer region, which changes RQ4), D14 (Sentinel-2 only as model input) and D16 (every 10 m pixel is classified, not every parcel). The current phases are described in the Research plan.

docs.title: Study area and data
docs.text:
Morocco. Five major agricultural regions that together span the country's diversity (Ouassanouan et al., 2026):

Region Climate Irrigation and crops El Gharb humid surface-water irrigation; rice, vegetables Tadla semi-arid to sub-humid large-scale irrigation; sugar beet, cereals Doukkala Mediterranean mixed irrigated and rainfed systems El Haouz semi-arid groundwater irrigation; olives, citrus Souss arid advanced drip systems; high-value export crops

Second study area. The proposal applied the best Morocco-trained model, without retraining, to Tunisia, validated with the GMIA-NEXT reference points (Kebede et al., 2026), which include only 10 rainfed points. Instead, Utah (USA) is studied as an independent second region with its own field-level labels (Water-Related Land Use, Utah Division of Water Resources), and it also provides the temporal test: models trained on 2024 are tested on 2021 (decision D13, Utah training data).

Data Use Field survey, Ouassanouan et al. (2026): 8,826 georeferenced parcels with crop type, irrigation status and irrigation system (8,781 after cleaning: 7,585 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed) training and validation in Morocco Sentinel-2 multispectral (10 m) and Sentinel-1 SAR (VV, VH) time series model input in the proposal; every model now uses Sentinel-2 only, Sentinel-1 remains an optional ablation (D14) GMIE, LGRIP30, FAO WaPOR, FAO AQUASTAT comparison of the maps with existing products and national statistics

docs.title: Models compared
docs.text: Six openly available GeoFMs are evaluated: Prithvi-EO-2.0 (NASA, IBM), Clay v1.5 (Clay Foundation), TerraMind (IBM, ESA), AgriFM (Li et al., 2025), Presto (Tseng et al., 2023) and TESSERA (Feng et al., 2025). The proposal named the first four; Presto and TESSERA, which encode the time series of a single pixel, were added later. Together they represent the principal GeoFM families: masked-autoencoder Vision Transformers, a multimodal generative model, an agriculture-specific spatio-temporal model and pixel time-series models. Every model receives Sentinel-2 input only (D14). Architecture, pretraining, configuration and sources are given in Foundation models.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
flowchart LR A["<b>1 · Data preparation</b><br/>Sentinel-2 time series<br/>labelled pixels · spatial folds"] --> B["<b>2 · Model evaluation</b><br/>frozen · LoRA · full fine-tuning · from scratch<br/>vs Sentinel-2 baselines"] B --> C["<b>3 · Temporal and spatial transferability</b><br/>Utah 2024 → 2021<br/>Morocco and Utah"] B -.-> E["<b>4 · Multi-model fusion</b><br/><i>optional</i>"] C --> D["<b>5 · Annual maps</b><br/>Morocco 2021–2025<br/>temporal consistency"]

The phases are described in the Research plan.

docs.title: Expected outcomes
docs.text:
1. A comprehensive evaluation of six geospatial foundation models for irrigated cropland mapping in North Africa, against a strong Sentinel-based baseline under spatial validation.
  2. A comparison of adaptation strategies for this task: frozen encoder, LoRA, full fine-tuning and training from scratch.
  3. Annual irrigated cropland maps for Morocco at 10 m resolution for 2021–2025, checked against national statistics.
  4. An assessment of the temporal consistency of foundation-model predictions across years.
  5. An assessment of how far the best model transfers to a data-scarce region.
  6. A reusable, ML-ready dataset of irrigated and rainfed parcels with spatial folds.

Full proposal

  • Prithvi on 10 m input (pretrained on 30 m HLS): state in thesis; optional 30 m ablation.
  • Neighbouring fields inside a chip (mixed 160 m patches, transformer context): add parcel "purity" + accuracy by parcel size; optional masked-chip ablation (MASK_OUTSIDE).
  • Per-year results (2023/24 vs 2024/25) from the out-of-fold predictions; year-transfer test within Doukkala / El Haouz.
  • ~~Tunisia: label source and transfer experiment~~ → replaced by Utah as a second study area (D13).
  • Utah: download WRLU 2024 tiles (SEASONS = ["2023/24"]), views, embeddings, RQ1 comparison; then 2021 and the temporal test (training script: train on one year, test on another).
  • Agree the new wording of RQ3 / RQ4 (D13) with the supervisors.
  • Prediction / wall-to-wall mapping step: STAC composites per block (s2_download/; cluster proxy access to the STAC hosts; reflectance offset from processing baseline 04.00), map of the best model, map accuracy sample (Olofsson et al. 2014).
  • Not-cropland samples are mostly easy (bare land, rangeland, riverside vegetation): false cropland inside the union mask has no label yet; consider a small labelled sample of union-only pixels.
  • Re-run 01_prepare_labels_* with the mask check once all masks exist (cluster).
  • Optional: ET (WaPOR), LST, precipitation (CHIRPS) as extra baseline variables, as ablations only.
  • Phase 2 (after Morocco is complete): US transfer study - see the change-log entry of 2026-11-04 (future phase). First step: one-day data check of the original state label sources.

docs.title: 2026-11-21 (E01 and E02 results, Morocco)
docs.text:
• E01 and E02 Morocco results copied from the cluster (experiments/E01_s2_pixel_baseline/results/morocco/, experiments/E02_temporal_nn/results/morocco/); comparison tables rebuilt (experiments/comparison/morocco/).
  • Results written on the E01 and E02 pages, the comparison page and Results: random forest 0.894, gradient boosting 0.893, TempCNN 0.912 macro-F1; no difference significant. Rainfed parcels lie almost only in Doukkala, Souss and Statte, which limits the rainfed scores.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (experiments redesigned: two classes, Morocco first)
docs.text:
• Decision D19: the experiments use two classes (irrigated, rainfed) on the surveyed parcel pixels; no cropland mask and no not-cropland class. Cropland extent and non-cropland handling move to the mapping phase.
  • pixelwise_run/: CLASSES = [1, 2] and headline macro_f1 in pixel_common.py (models output two scores, metrics, class weights, confusion follow it); 04_make_pixel_samples.py samples parcel pixels only, into 04_pixel_samples/ (Morocco: 473,675 pixels of 8,775 parcels; the old 3-class samples stay in 04c_pixel_samples/); 01_prepare_labels_* no longer check the mask; the parcel mask helper cropland_mask.py removed; E05 label subsets without not-cropland pixels.
  • Experiments: E02 runs TempCNN only (pixel L-TAE on hold); the seed also sets the initial weights in E02; E05 moved from Utah to Morocco; every script, report.py, report_figures.py and 05_compare_experiments.py on 2 classes and Morocco first. Quick tests of E01–E05 passed on the Mac.
  • All earlier pixel-wise results (3 classes) removed from the repository (experiments/E0*/results/, comparison tables, result figures); experiment pages rewritten as plans with collapsible explanations of every model.
  • cropland_extent/download_dynamic_world.py: annual Dynamic World layer per agricultural year (most frequent class, mean crop probability, image count) on the project grid, for the later choice of a mask.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (experiments renumbered: E03 U-TAE, E04 frozen GeoFMs)
docs.text: • E03 and E04 swapped so the numbering follows the logic of the study: E01 simple classifiers, E02 temporal network on pixels (TempCNN), E03 U-TAE (temporal network on tiles, from scratch), E04 frozen GeoFMs + decoder, E05 fine-tuning. Folders experiments/E03_utae/, experiments/E04_frozen_geofm/, pages, figures (confusion_e04.png), comparison tables (paired_vs_E03_utae_utae.csv) and all current pages renamed. Older change-log entries and meeting notes keep the numbers of their time (there, E03 = frozen GeoFMs, E04 = U-TAE).

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (pixel L-TAE on hold; comparison page)
docs.text:
• The pixel-wise L-TAE of E02 is on hold (set-up under review): left out of 05_compare_experiments.py (EXCLUDE), the figures (experiments/report_figures.py) and every page; E02 reports TempCNN only. The Holm family of the E01–E04 tests now has seven runs; the p-values were recomputed (conclusions unchanged).
  • New page Comparison of the experiments: all runs of E01–E04, paired tests against the random forest and U-TAE, findings. The E03 page now reports only its four encoders (new figure confusion_e03.png), with a collapsible explanation of UPerNet; E02 has one for TempCNN.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (E05: LoRA added as a fourth strategy)
docs.text:
• E05 now compares four strategies: frozen, LoRA, full fine-tuning and from scratch (16 jobs; the 4 LoRA jobs run later). LoRA: rank 16, α 32, on the qkv, fc1 and fc2 layers of all 24 Prithvi blocks (5.51 M adapter weights + 2.48 M head), adapters at the head's learning rate 10⁻⁴, as Marti-Escofet et al. (2025) for Prithvi. Local quick test passed (about 1.3 × the frozen time per epoch).
  • GeoFMSegmenter(lora_targets=...) chooses the adapted layers; report.py adds LoRA − frozen, fine-tuned − LoRA and LoRA − scratch to the paired tests (Holm over 24 comparisons per metric).

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (documentation)
docs.text:
• RQ2 · Fine-tuning: six ways to adapt a GeoFM (frozen, full, partial, PEFT, LP-FT, continued pretraining), figures (strategies, animation, LoRA), workflow, and six papers to read.
  • Foundation models: configuration rewritten for the pixel-wise set-up (tiles, head, frozen / LoRA / fine-tuned per experiment); the parcel-wise chip set-up kept as an archived subsection.

  • Phase 3 renamed "Temporal and spatial transferability".
  • Whole documentation checked against the pixel-wise state; parcel-wise material kept and labelled as archived: the Phase 2 workflow, models pipeline and parcel-level evaluation protocol moved to the archive; new Phase 2 overview and pixel-wise evaluation protocol; Results, research plan and decisions updated (D5, D6, D8, D11 marked as parcel-wise or superseded; new D18, STAC composites for the maps); Phase 1 pages (pixel samples of all sets, Utah status, STAC tiles), Phases 3–5, setup, data sources, introduction and the reference pages brought up to date.
  • New weekly page 2026-W47; progress report rewritten.
  • Reference pages: Tomotaki-Dawoud et al. (2025) (authors and DOI corrected in the index) and TESSERA.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (STAC download: crash fixed, safe logs)
docs.text:
• Utah 2023/24: 29 of 32 parts finished (17,278 of 18,472 tiles, all readable); 3 parts crashed, leaving 78 blocks. Cause: stackstac leaves out scenes whose footprint does not reach the block, but the reflectance offsets were taken from all search results. Offsets are now matched to the stacked scenes by id.
  • Each part writes its own logs (logs/); the last part merges them into tiles_qa.jsonl, blocks_done.jsonl and blocks_failed.jsonl (32 processes appending to one file over NFS had lost 19 QA rows).
  • New wrapper s2_download/s2_dl.sbatch (several parts per job) fails if any part fails; usage and memory (about 6 GB per part) in its header.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (E05: Prithvi frozen vs fine-tuned vs from scratch)
docs.text:
• New experiment E05 (experiments/E05_prithvi_strategies/run.py, report.py), Utah: the E03 Prithvi network with the encoder frozen, fully fine-tuned (encoder learning rate 10⁻⁵) or trained from random weights, each with 10 / 25 / 50 / 100% of the training-fold parcels.
  • tile_common.py: GeoFMSegmenter(frozen=False, pretrained=...) trains every encoder weight; label_subset keeps a nested, per-class share of the training parcels (validation and test folds unchanged); the training loop logs validation loss and cropland macro-F1 per epoch, gives the encoder its own learning rate, optional warm-up and gradient clipping, and keeps trained encoder weights in the best model; the seed is set before each model is built. encoders.Prithvi.load_encoder(pretrained=False) builds the random-weight encoder.
  • 05_compare_experiments.py reads E01–E04 only, so their Holm family and p-values stay as reported.
  • LoRA moved out of the RQ2 plan: E05 compares full fine-tuning with frozen and from scratch; LoRA can be added later.

docs.title: 2026-11-20 (STAC download: parity mode removed)
docs.text: • The STAC approach is independent of the Earth Engine tiles (its models are trained on STAC tiles only), so the parity mode of s2_download/02_download_s2_stac.py and 03_parity_check.py were removed; 02 now downloads every cropland tile of the mask. Morocco 2024/25 added; S2_SEASONS selects the year per cluster job.

docs.title: 2026-11-19 (E03 and E04 results)
docs.text:
• E04 U-TAE and E03 with Prithvi, Clay, TerraMind and AgriFM finished in both regions; result pages written (E03, E04). Utah: U-TAE +0.037 and the foundation models +0.055 to +0.068 cropland macro-F1 over the random forest, three encoders also significantly above U-TAE. Morocco: no significant difference on the cropland metric.
  • 05_compare_experiments.py also tests every run against E04 U-TAE (paired_vs_E04_utae_utae.csv); the Holm family now holds the eight runs of E01–E04, so the E01 / E02 pages were updated to the final p-values.

docs.title: 2026-11-19 (pixel-wise set-up: cropland mask, pixel samples, experiment plan)
docs.text:
• AlphaEarth removed from the pixel-wise experiments (the embedding experiment and its Earth Engine sampling script; AlphaEarth publishes embeddings only, no weights to fine-tune). Experiments renumbered: E03 frozen foundation models + decoder, E04 U-TAE, E05 LoRA (run order E01, E02, E04, E03, E05); pipeline steps 05 comparison, 06 wall-to-wall tiles. The AlphaEarth papers stay in the references as related work.
  • Code folders reorganised into two independent pipelines, scripts numbered in run order.
  • pixelwise_run/ (current): 01 labels, 02 folds, 03 tiles (+ 03b quicklooks), 04 pixel samples (was 04c_make_pixel_samples.py), 05 comparison of experiments, 06 wall-to-wall tiles (was 03c_build_cropland_tiles.py); helper modules regions.py, cropland_mask.py, pixel_common.py, nn_common.py, tile_common.py, encoders.py (all six foundation models; the four image models with the same weights and bands as the archived embedding scripts).
  • parcelwise_run/ (archive): 01–03 (copies), 04 views, 05 inspection, 06a–06d embeddings, 07 / 07b / 07c training, 08 comparison, 09 breakdown, with experiment_utils.py; experiments/parcel_wise_classification/ and jobs/embed_*.sbatch, jobs/make_views.sbatch point there.
  • ml_dataset_prep/ and models_run/ no longer exist. Output folders keep their names (04c_pixel_samples, 03c_cropland_tiles_128px), so existing data stays valid. cropland_extent/ stays (step 0).
  • Two more foundation models: Presto and TESSERA v2 (Medium), pixel time-series models with open weights (Presto MIT; TESSERA weights CC0). Loaders in experiments/pixel_encoders.py (code cloned to external/presto, external/tessera; weights in checkpoints/presto/default_model.pt, checkpoints/tessera/ckpt/student_medium.pt). Both are E03 / E05 encoders like the other four: every pixel of a tile is encoded (128-d), the 10 m map goes to the same UPerNet head; Sentinel-2 only (Presto: S1 / ERA5 / SRTM / Dynamic World tokens masked; TESSERA: empty Sentinel-1 branch). LoRA on TESSERA's feed-forward layers (its attention packs q, k, v). Checked on a small tile subset on the Mac. Pages: Foundation models, E03, E05 (deferred).
  • Experiment scripts E01–E05 in experiments/ (one folder per experiment with run.py): shared code pixel_common.py (samples, features, PASTIS rotation, metrics, block bootstrap from per-block confusion matrices), nn_common.py (L-TAE, TempCNN, MLP), tile_common.py (tile data, frozen / LoRA foundation-model segmenter with L-TAE and UPerNet head, U-TAE), 05_compare_experiments.py (comparison table, paired tests with Holm correction); Every script was run on a small subset on the Mac. One page per experiment in the Experiments menu; the menu is called "Experiments" and the pixel-wise experiments are numbered E01–E05 (the parcel-wise ones stay "archived E01–E05").
  • Imagery source for the maps: the experiments E01–E05 use the existing Earth Engine tiles; the wall-to-wall composites for the maps are planned from STAC per 10.24 km block, after a benchmark and a parity check against the Earth Engine tiles (plan). Utah 2020/21 tiles downloaded on the cluster (2,716 tiles).
  • New folder cropland_extent/ with make_cropland_mask.py (before pixelwise_run/00_make_cropland_mask.py), download_esa_worldcover.py and download_lgrip30.py (before tools/a7_…, tools/a8_…). All three write to outputs/<region>/cropland_extent/ (cropland_mask/<season>/, esa_worldcover/, lgrip30/) and use the region's mapping area of regions.py (map_file, map_where; new helpers map_area(), cropland_dir(), mask_dir()).
  • Cropland mask (page, D17): union of 4 products in Earth Engine, downloaded in 1024 px blocks on the tile grid (0.5 s per block), one VRT per year, vote count and per-product bit flags kept, tile table with the cropland pixels per 128 px tile. GCEP30 continental tiles combined with max() (the overlapping tiles disagree in Morocco). Dynamic World dropped (25 s per block, Earth Engine memory errors). 2023/24: Morocco 103,068 km² (24.8%), Utah 9,979 km² (4.5%). No parcel data is read by the mask script.
  • Labels: 01_prepare_labels_* read the mask of each parcel's year through pixelwise_run/cropland_mask.py and add mask_frac, mask_votes, in_mask, mask_<product> and mask_check.csv; this replaces the WorldCover check (wc_cropland_frac, wc_major). Parcels outside the mask are kept.
  • 06_build_cropland_tiles.py (new): wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles (12 months × 13 bands) for every 128 px tile with cropland, same grid and compositing as 03; parcel-store tiles copied (identical to a fresh download). Tested on 16 tiles (1.7 s per tile, 2.8 MB); not run: Morocco needs 132,616 tiles (~370 GB per year), Utah 24,861 (~69 GB); download deferred to the mapping stage.
  • 04_make_pixel_samples.py (new): labelled pixels (irrigated, rainfed, not cropland) with folds from the parcel tile store and the mask (page); Morocco 2023/24: 402,756 pixels.
  • WorldCover and LGRIP30 PNG maps with legend and AOI boundary (MAKE_PNG, PNG_ONLY); WorldCover with its official palette.
  • Docs: new pages Cropland extent and mask, Pixel samples and Pixel-wise experiment plan; decisions D16 and D17; Phase 1 overview, data sources (Esri LULC, GCEP30, GLAD now used), experiments overview; the parcel-wise plan marked as archived; tools/a6_copy_doc_figures.py copies the new figures and the archived E01 figures from their new paths.
  • Cluster: pulled to aca6eb1; masks for all four years running on the login node (Earth Engine needs the internet; compute nodes have none); then labels, pixel samples and copy of the small results to the Mac.

docs.title: 2026-11-18 (parcel-wise experiments archived)
docs.text:

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (review before running E02–E05: fixes)
docs.text: An independent code review (no data leakage found; draws identical across scripts; E02 and E03 inputs identical, checked) and a docs check led to these fixes: - Quick checks (QUICK_TEST, QUICK = True) write to experiments/<E>/results_quick/ and write no report; before, a quick run left oof_predictions.csv in the real folder and the real run would have been skipped. - Nested label-efficiency draws: one random order of the blocks per region, round and draw; a fraction takes its first blocks (10% ⊂ 25% ⊂ 50%), accepted if the first 10% hold ≥ 20 rainfed parcels. - Single-seed curve points: 03b and 03c save oof_per_seed.csv; the 100% point of a neural learning curve is the mean over its seeds scored one by one, like the single-seed label-efficiency runs. Training parcels per fraction are reported. - 04: the Holm family is the experiment's own runs only; new paired table differences_vs_earlier_experiments.csv (same input, this experiment's head vs the earlier experiments' heads: E03 vs E02, E04 vs E03 and E02); a borrowed experiment without runs or a missing baseline stops the script; development-mode paths built after the region override. - 05: reports every head (the filter dropped MLP / L-TAE / PSE-TAE); runs without a baseline (E05). - Runners: run_experiment.py and submit_slurm.py drop stray EXPERIMENT_* shell variables and set every run variable explicitly; submit_slurm.py submits a compare job only when the borrowed experiments are finished (or WAIT_FOR). - E04 config: HEAD: ltae (it would have run the MLP head); breakdown step added to E02–E05. - Report: sections for the head-vs-head table, spread over seeds, L-TAE attention per month, permutation importance, training curves and results by zone. - Docs: seeds (42, 1042, 2042), L-TAE time encoding, E04 implementation section, results-page contents (PCA explained variance dropped; crop-group breakdown and compute cost marked as later / by hand), status table.

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (code for E02–E05 in both regions, with label efficiency)
docs.text:
• New models_run/experiment_utils.py: region paths, environment overrides (EXPERIMENT_REGION, _INPUT, _FRACTION, _DRAW, _N_SEEDS, _QUICK_TEST) and the label-efficiency block draw (draw_training_blocks(): blocks with and without rainfed parcels drawn separately, ≥ 20 rainfed parcels, seed from region / round / fraction / draw only, so draws are identical in scripts 03, 03b, 03c and for every input; only parcels of the views' years).
  • 03_train_evaluate.py: REGION / VIEWS_NAME (Utah file names _2023-24), gradient boosting removed, TRAIN_FRACTION / FRACTION_DRAW (label-efficiency runs skip random-vs-spatial CV, final models and importance), results to experiments/<E>/results/<region>/.
  • 03b_train_psetae.py: N_SEEDS = 3 trainings per round (mean probability; metrics_per_seed.csv), label efficiency.
  • New 03c_train_ltae.py: HEAD = "mlp" (E03, MLP on the PCA input) and HEAD = "ltae" (E04, L-TAE + MLP), 3 seeds, label efficiency, same output format as script 03; L-TAE attention per month and class.
  • 04_compare_models.py: per region; EXTRA_RUNS may be "<experiment>/*"; differs now requires the CI to exclude 0 and Holm p < 0.05 (protocol §8; ci_excludes_0 kept); learning curves (learning_curve.csv / .png).
  • 05_breakdown_oof.py: per region (focus zone and irrigated-only zones per region; focus_zone.csv).
  • run_experiment.py: loops over regions, inputs and label-efficiency runs (plan_runs()), compare / breakdown per region, QUICK mode. New experiments/submit_slurm.py: one Slurm job per run (jobs/step_cpu.sbatch, jobs/step_gpu.sbatch), then a compare job per region.
  • make_report.py: one section per region (tables, figures with the region in the file name, learning curves); E01's single-region layout still read.
  • Configs: E03 / E04 / E05 compare with earlier experiments (EXTRA_RUNS); E05 runs both regions and has compare and report steps.
  • Docs: models pipeline §6.6–6.8 (regions and label efficiency, script 03c, script 03b), §7 (Holm rule, regions, learning curves), §7.1, §8, §9; experiment pages (how to run, order); SERVER.md §3.3b; models_run/README.md.

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (how the models handle time)
docs.text: • Models pipeline §5.2 (new): how Clay, TerraMind, Prithvi (4 months per pass, one embedding per month) and AgriFM (12 months merged to one time step inside the network) handle the 12 months, with the consequences for E02–E04 and the AgriFM temporal-resolution limitation. File format moved to §5.3. Flowchart: AgriFM normalisation and 2 × 2 grid.

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (label efficiency inside E02–E05; no separate E06)
docs.text:

Same 270 runs in total.
  • label_efficiency block added to the E02–E05 configs; label-efficiency section and references (Mughees et al. 2026; Brown et al. 2025) added to their setup pages; plan §6 rewritten ("Label efficiency (inside E02–E05)"), §9–§11 updated. The E06 folders were moved to tmp_trash/E06_label_efficiency_retired/.

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (E06 covers every experiment)
docs.text:

It also shows whether the best head and PCA vs L-TAE change when labels are few. Config (repeat_experiments, seeds_per_draw), setup page and plan §6, §9–§11 updated.

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (experiments renumbered in run order; "PASTIS validation" dropped from the names)
docs.text:

Change-log entries before 2026-11-13 and the meeting notes keep the old numbers (folder links updated).

docs.title: 2026-11-13 (experiment pages: titles and references)

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (embeddings for two regions; AgriFM normalisation)
docs.text:
• Scripts 02a–02d: new settings REGION and VIEWS_NAME (environment variables EMBED_REGION, EMBED_VIEWS); chips are read from outputs/<REGION>/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/<VIEWS_NAME>/ and embeddings written to outputs/<REGION>/study/02_embeddings/. Decision D15. Morocco chip statistics: blue 714 ± 344 … SWIR2 2,471 ± 953.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (RQ1 experiment plan)
docs.text:
• New page RQ1 · Experiment plan (Phase 2): decisions, shared settings, inputs, design (input × temporal handling × head), E02 PCA + LogReg/RF/SVM, E05 PCA + MLP, E03 L-TAE + MLP, E04 PSE-TAE, E06 label efficiency, ablations A1–A5 (incl. a location-shortcut test for Clay and Prithvi), analyses, the tables and figures of every experiment's report page, order of work and number of runs.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (Sentinel-2 only for every input, D14)
docs.text:
• Decision D14: all inputs of the model comparison use Sentinel-2 only; Sentinel-1 becomes an optional ablation in Morocco.
  • models_run/03_train_evaluate.py: S1S2_VARIABLES = "s2" by default. With Sentinel-2 only the orbit plays no role and is left out of the run name (s1s2-s2_agyear_tiles-inner).
  • models_run/02c_embed_terramind.py: MODALITIES = ["S2L2A"] by default; the output is terramind_agyear_tiles.npz for Sentinel-2 only and terramind-s1s2_agyear_tiles.npz with Sentinel-1 (INPUT = "terramind-s1s2" in script 03). With Sentinel-2 only, a month counts as valid only if it has clear Sentinel-2 pixels (before, Sentinel-1 data alone also made a month valid).
  • The existing local TerraMind embeddings (made with Sentinel-1) were renamed to terramind-s1s2_agyear_tiles.npz (and _parts_terramind-s1s2_agyear_tiles/); TerraMind must be embedded again with Sentinel-2 only. The cluster copy still has the old name.
  • models_run/03b_train_psetae.py: BANDS = "s2" by default. E04 runs morocco_s2 and utah_s2; morocco_s2s1 stays as the Sentinel-1 ablation, utah_s2s1 is no longer run.
  • models_run/04_compare_models.py: baseline run s1s2-s2_agyear_tiles-inner (experiment mode picks the Sentinel-2 baseline first); PSE-TAE run psetae_morocco_views_s2.
  • E02 and E03 configs: Sentinel-2 baseline. Docs: foundation models table (baseline 180 features), models pipeline.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (PSE-TAE baseline for two regions: one config file per run)
docs.text:
• models_run/03b_train_psetae.py reads the region and the views folder from the settings (REGION, VIEWS_NAME) instead of fixed Morocco paths. The input paths are built after the config file has been read, so a config that sets the region also changes the pixel sets and the folds that are read. The run name now carries the region, the views folder and the band set (psetae_<REGION>_<VIEWS_NAME>_<BANDS>), so runs of the two regions no longer overwrite each other.
  • New setting CONFIG (or the environment variable PSETAE_CONFIG): one file in experiments/E05_psetae_scratch/configs/ holds all settings of one run. Four files define the four runs: morocco_s2, morocco_s2s1, utah_s2, utah_s2s1 (Sentinel-2 only vs Sentinel-2 + Sentinel-1; Morocco views with the ascending orbit, Utah views_2023-24 with the descending orbit). Unknown setting names stop the run.
  • experiments/run_experiment.py: the psetae step runs once per file listed in psetae_configs of the experiment's config.yaml. E04 lists the four files; the report step is left out until make_report.py handles two regions in one experiment.
  • Config files are read as UTF-8 in 03_train_evaluate.py, 03b_train_psetae.py, 04_compare_models.py and run_experiment.py: Slurm jobs on the cluster run without a UTF-8 locale, and the first four PSE-TAE jobs stopped on a non-ASCII character in a config comment.
  • Checked with QUICK_TEST on Morocco (s2 and s2s1, 3 epochs, then deleted) and a path check for Utah. The earlier E04 run (results/psetae_agyear_s2s1) is kept unchanged. Model, folds and metrics are unchanged.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (tile quick-looks; tile store check on the cluster; Utah 2023/24 tiles downloaded)
docs.text:
• New script ml_dataset_prep/03b_tile_quicklooks.py: one figure per tile (monthly true colour, NDVI, Sentinel-1 VH, label rasters, mean NDVI and VH per class); documented in Morocco training data §6.7.
  • Utah 2023/24 tiles downloaded on the cluster: 2,720 of 2,720 tiles (9.1 GB).
  • Check of every downloaded tile of both regions (band order, data type, grid, label consistency with parcels.csv, value ranges, missing-data consistency, parcel completeness): Morocco 2,987 tiles without errors; Utah only isolated off-parcel pixel flags (single-band Sentinel-2 gaps in one month, one permanent strong radar reflector). Parcels absent from the label rasters: Morocco 6 (covered by an overlapping parcel), Utah 2 (slivers below 0.13 ha whose pixels collide with a neighbouring parcel).
  • Utah 2023/24 Sentinel-1 is descending only (ascending data in 273 of 2,720 tiles, median 0 months), a consequence of the Sentinel-1A-only acquisition plan after the loss of Sentinel-1B; the Utah views have to use the descending orbit.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (Utah: second study area, years 2024 + 2021)
docs.text:
• D13: Utah is an independent second study area (no Morocco → Utah transfer); RQ3 temporal test in Utah: train on WRLU 2024 (2023/24), test on WRLU 2021 (2020/21) on the held-out folds. D10, Phase 3, the research plan, the introduction and the progress report reworded.
  • Label change between years for all labelled crop fields of WRLU, compared with 2024 (outputs/utah/dataset/01_labels/year_change_vs_2024.csv): crops change 27–41%, class 0.01–0.07% since 2021, 1.35% in 2019 (sudden jump, possibly a revision of the mapping); 2025 repeats 94% of the 2024 crops.
  • 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py: YEARS = [2024, 2021]. Re-run 01, 02 and 03 (plan only): 12,015 fields in 550 cells (2024: 5,000 irrigated + 1,013 rainfed; 2021: 4,987 + 1,015), 183 blocks, 5,436 tiles (2,720 + 2,716). The earlier 2024 + 2025 label rasters were removed (tmp_trash/).
  • Utah training data rewritten with the full design: study design, choice of years, the label-change table, sampling algorithm (cells, strata, block cap, seed), what is labelled in a tile, why a sample, one tile per place and year, temporal test (scores A, B, C), running one year at a time, limitations.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (Utah training data; one pipeline for two regions; outputs per region)
docs.text:
• Transfer region = Utah (WRLU, Utah Division of Water Resources), see D10 and Utah training data. Data copied to data/Utah_field_data/ (WRLU 2017–2025).
  • One pipeline for both regions.
  • ml_dataset_prep/01_prepare_labels.py renamed 01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py; new 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py. Both write the same file layout and columns.
  • New ml_dataset_prep/regions.py: the settings that differ per region (projection, first month of the agricultural year, block size, map boundaries). Scripts 02–04 and models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py have REGION = "morocco" | "utah" at the top.
  • Admin boundaries now FAO GAUL (data/admin_boundaries/: 2015 level 0 for Morocco, 2024 level 1 for the US states), replacing GADM; the region's features are cached in outputs/<region>/dataset/admin_boundaries.geojson.
  • Field survey moved to data/Morocco_field_survey/.
  • Outputs per region: outputs/morocco/{dataset, study, analysis} (all existing outputs, moved unchanged) and outputs/utah/dataset. Paths updated in ml_dataset_prep/, models_run/, tools/, experiments/make_report.py. The HPC copy still uses the old layout (outputs/dataset, outputs/study); it must be moved the same way before the next sync (only when asked).
  • Morocco unchanged: steps 01–03 (03 without download) re-run into a scratch folder give identical parcels, folds, blocks and tile plan (8,781 parcels, 2,987 tiles).
  • 02_make_spatial_folds.py: the class-similarity curve uses only pairs of the same agricultural year (the same Utah field in two years is not two samples). Folds are not affected.
  • One year at a time (SEASONS setting): 03_build_tiles.py still plans and writes label rasters for every year in the parcel file (parcel numbers and tile index never change), but downloads only the years in SEASONS; 04_make_views.py builds views of the years in SEASONS into their own folder (views_2023-24/), views/ when SEASONS = None (all years, as for Morocco). models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py: new setting VIEWS_NAME. Tested without download (Utah) and on 50 Moroccan parcels of 2024/25 (scratch folder).
  • 02_make_spatial_folds.py now also draws spatial_folds_blocks.png: the blocks coloured by fold, with the fold number in each block and zooms on the N_ZOOMS densest windows of ZOOM_BLOCKS × ZOOM_BLOCKS blocks. The Moroccan figure of the same name was made by hand earlier; a re-run of 02 for Morocco replaces it with this one.
  • Utah dataset (WRLU 2024 → 2023/24, 2025 → 2024/25; water year 1 Oct – 30 Sep):
  • labels: Flood / Sprinkler / Drip / Pivot / Wheel = irrigated, Dry Crop = rainfed; Sub-irrigated dropped; crop groups grain/seeds, hay/turf, field crops. WRLU 2025 split Sprinkler into Sprinkler / Pivot / Wheel; the first run missed Pivot and Wheel (20,000 fewer irrigated fields in 2025) and was corrected.
  • sampling: 550 cells of 1.28 km (400 with rainfed, 150 irrigated only; ≤ 6 per 20 km block), all fields inside → 11,804 fields (9,728 irrigated, 2,076 rainfed, 17.6%).
  • folds: class similarity reaches the random level at 15–20 km → 20 km blocks (193 blocks).
  • tile plan: 5,603 tiles, label rasters written; Sentinel download not yet run.
  • only 14 of 5,850 fields change class between 2024 and 2025 → temporal tests must also hold out space.
  • a run of 01 at 15:33 gave 11,806 fields; runs in condaml give 11,804 every time (one rainfed alfalfa field, UT2024_62293 / UT2025_62293, fewer). The difference probably comes from another GDAL / GEOS version. The current files come from condaml (11,804); 02 and 03 (plan) were re-run from them. Run the pipeline in condaml only.
  • 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py step 4b (EXPORT_ALL_FIELDS): all labelled crop fields before sampling (2024: 107,348 irrigated + 15,276 rainfed; 2025: 108,536 + 15,186) -> all_crop_fields.gpkg with a column sampled, all_fields_summary.csv, all_fields_by_zone.csv and figures (map per year, class balance and size, crops). The sample holds 4.5% of the irrigated and 6.8% of the rainfed fields.

docs.title: 2026-11-12 (results by region and purity; AgriFM input scale examined)
docs.text:
• What: new script models_run/05_breakdown_oof.py splits the out-of-fold predictions of an experiment by zone, agricultural year, 16-px patch purity and parcel area, with Doukkala-only macro-F1 and the false-rainfed rate in the irrigated-only zones (block-bootstrap CIs). Run on E01; results in experiments/E01_frozen_pca_nested/results/breakdown/. Described in Frozen encoders §7.1.
  • Why: a review of the dataset found that the class is confounded with the region (94% of the rainfed parcels in Doukkala) and that 78% of the parcels have a 16-px patch purity below 0.5.
  • Finding (E01): in Doukkala no frozen GeoFM exceeds the baseline; the GeoFM advantage in the hardest fold comes from the 69 rainfed parcels of Souss.
  • AgriFM: the normalisation statistics of configs/cropland_mapping.py do not match the Earth Engine composites (blue: chips 728 ± 344, config 4,179 ± 4,042). The AgriFM paper does not report its normalisation; its pretraining is supervised on GLC_FCS30D land-cover fractions, with 5-day Sentinel-2 series (16 frames per sample).

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (reference summary: GMIA-NEXT)
docs.text: • New summary page GMIA-NEXT · Kebede et al. (2026) from the preprint, the Zenodo records (maps 17627111, points 20732681) and the code repository: method, reference points, accuracy per continent, data records, use in this research (independent test points, comparison map) and limitations (30 m, interpreted labels, 45 m clustering only, preprint). Reference row marked ★ and linked; Data sources row linked.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (AgriFM weights were not loaded; fixed)
docs.text:
• What: models_run/02d_embed_agrifm.py loads AgriFM.pth by name (prefix encoder. removed, S2_patch_emd → patch_emd.proj) and stops unless every encoder tensor loads; patch size 4 × 4 × 4 px (the pretrained patch embedding), output stride 32 px (STRIDE_PX = 32); a check stops the run if the feature grid does not match the stride. Decision D12.
  • Why: the AgriFM embeddings on the local machine and on the cluster disagreed (cosine similarity ≈ 0.05 against ≈ 1.0 for TerraMind). The cause: no pretrained weight had been loaded (mmengine reported success despite the mismatch), so all earlier AgriFM embeddings, including E01, came from a randomly initialised encoder.
  • Where: AgriFM re-embedded and re-trained on the cluster; old outputs kept as *_random_init on the cluster.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (setup on the UT EEMCS HPC cluster)
docs.text:
• What: repository cloned to the UT EEMCS HPC cluster (~/irrimapping-geofm), conda environment condaml built with the CUDA build of PyTorch (tested on an NVIDIA L40 node), input data and the 128 px tile dataset copied; model weights are downloaded on the cluster on first use.
  • Why: the embedding and training runs need a GPU.
  • Where: SERVER.md in the project root (connection, environment, data transfer, Slurm job scripts).

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (content from the results presentation of week 45)
docs.text: Only content that is still valid for the current pipeline was taken over; numbers from the earlier 30-day pipeline were not. - E01 report: new section Additional analyses from the E01 result files — random vs spatial CV (all inputs), grouped permutation importance of the baseline (variables and months) with figure, settings selected per round. - RQ1 page §6.2: principle and fixed settings of each classifier (L2/lbfgs, 500 trees, HGB early stopping off and why, SVM without probability calibration). - Evaluation protocol: why a fold rotation instead of one fixed split; no kappa (Pontius & Millones 2011); block bootstrap (Künsch 1989). - ML-ready dataset §6.2: crop calendar and the reasons for the September–August agricultural year. - References: Valavi 2019, Schratz 2019, Karasiak 2022, Orynbaikyzy 2022, Künsch 1989, Gao 2018, Elwan 2022. - tools/a6_copy_doc_figures.py also copies the two E01 figures.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (reference summary: Moroccan field survey)
docs.text: • New summary page Moroccan field survey · Ouassanouan et al. (2026) (from the paper PDF): protocol, attributes, data records (figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.28486022.v2), quality control, use in this research, limitations (rainfed concentrated in Doukkala, region–season confounding, route-based sampling, single-season labels). Linked from the reference table, the menu and Data sources.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (documentation organised by research phase)
docs.text:

Decisions moved to decisions.md; the method/ folder is gone (old copies in tmp_trash/pre_phase_move/).

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (Method section reordered; dataset figures in the documentation)
docs.text:

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (diagram labels no longer cut off)
docs.text: • Diagram text was clipped in some browsers (e.g. "Dec 2023 – Jan 202"): labels were measured with a fallback font and drawn with the site font. docs/assets/javascripts/mermaid.js now waits for the web font and uses the site font (Roboto); extra.css fixes the label font and shows any overflow. Checked: all 25 diagrams, no clipped label.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (Foundation models page; academic register)
docs.text:

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (model weights in checkpoints/, downloaded on the first run)
docs.text:

AgriFM already used checkpoints/agrifm/. Copies of the old scripts in tmp_trash/.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (diagrams: one neutral academic style, readable size)

Result: all 26 diagrams fit the page, none scrolls. Gantt timeline sized to the column.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (introduction from the proposal; data sources; reference papers; progress report)

Home page: no names, no workflow (moved to Method in brief), generic research wording across the site.

docs.text: • New one-paragraph thesis description (from the proposal) in README.md and docs/index.md, replacing the method-oriented summary.

docs.title: 2026-11-06 (all documentation in docs/, served by MkDocs; CLAUDE.md)
docs.text:
• One documentation folder. Every page now lives in docs/ (MkDocs docs_dir); moved with links rewritten: README → docs/index.md (home) + docs/setup.md (setup, run order, structure); docs/0x_*.md → docs/research/ (thesis_design, overview, protocol, decisions, literature); ml_dataset_prep/README.md → docs/dataset/index.md; models_run/README.md → docs/models/index.md; experiment README / REPORT → docs/experiments/<name>/index.md (setup) and report.md, figures in docs/experiments/<name>/figures/; PROGRESS.md → docs/progress.md; docs/05_results.md → docs/results.md. Hand-written breadcrumbs and previous / next lines removed (the site draws them). Old files in tmp_trash/pre_docs_migration/.

The mkdocs-gen-files mirror (mkdocs/gen_pages.py) is no longer needed and was removed; style and Mermaid script in docs/assets/.
