docs.title: 2026-11-06 (documentation website with MkDocs; D11 heads and mapping)
docs.text:
• MkDocs Material website replaces the hand-built HTML (docs/build_site.py, docs/site/ moved to tmp_trash/old_html_site/). mkdocs.yml (root) + mkdocs/gen_pages.py (mkdocs-gen-files): the markdown files stay where they are; at build time they are mirrored into the site at the same paths, so links work the same on GitHub and on the site; images copied; links to scripts / tables / folders point to GitHub; navigation (tabs: Home, Research, Results, Meetings, Code reference) written from the experiment configs (mkdocs-literate-nav). Anchors use GitHub's slugs (pymdownx.slugs). Mermaid rendered by mkdocs/pages/javascripts/mermaid.js (keeps the diagram colours). .github/workflows/docs.yml rebuilds and publishes to GitHub Pages on every push to main. environment.yml: mkdocs<2, mkdocs-material, mkdocs-gen-files, mkdocs-literate-nav. .gitignore: site/. make_report.py: <details markdown="1"> so the collapsed table renders on both. Checked: build without warnings; 19 pages, 26 Mermaid diagrams, no broken internal links or anchors.
  • D11 (docs/04_decisions.md): parcel benchmark with classical heads for RQ1; for the maps (RQ2–RQ4) frozen GeoFM + UPerNet on the tile label pixels, RF on per-pixel S1/S2 features, and neural baselines TempCNN (pixel) and U-TAE (tile); pixel predictions aggregated per parcel for the same scoring. Literature table added to docs/research/README.md (references checked against the papers).

docs.title: 2026-11-05 (project organised: experiments, documentation hierarchy, HTML site)
docs.text:
• Experiments. New experiments/: one folder per experiment with config.yaml (all settings, same names as the scripts), README.md (question, why, what changes, how to run), REPORT.md (answer first; tables and figures generated) and results/. run_experiment.py runs the steps of a config (train_evaluate per input, compare, report), skips finished runs and saves config + git commit + dates in results/run_info.json. make_report.py writes the tables (macro-F1 per input × classifier, differences vs baseline with Holm verdict, per-class metrics with CI, macro-F1 per fold) and two figures into REPORT.md, and refreshes experiments/README.md and docs/05_results.md. Template in experiments/_template/.
  • Experiment mode in the scripts. models_run/03_train_evaluate.py, 03b_train_psetae.py, 04_compare_models.py: new setting EXPERIMENT (None = as before, results in outputs/study/). When set (or by run_experiment.py), the config's section replaces the settings, unknown names stop the run, results go to experiments/<name>/results/; finished runs are skipped. 03: derived paths moved below the override; no _nested suffix inside an experiment. 04: compares all runs of the experiment, baseline found automatically, EXTRA_RUNS adds runs of other experiments (PCA vs L-TAE); figure title names the experiment.
  • Runs moved: the five runs of 30 Oct (nested CV) from outputs/study/03_models/ to experiments/E01_frozen_pca_nested/results/, compared and reported (8,775 common parcels); the PSE-TAE run to experiments/E05_psetae_scratch/results/ (parked, listed: false).
  • E01 result: no GeoFM differs from the baseline after Holm for Clay, Prithvi, TerraMind; AgriFM worse (RF, SVM). Best: Clay + SVM 0.910, baseline SVM 0.906. Fold 0 (rainfed in Doukkala + Souss): baseline 0.80, Clay and Prithvi higher with every classifier.
  • Planned: E02 (PASTIS validation, ready) and E03 (L-TAE pipeline; design in its README and in the protocol §5).
  • Documentation hierarchy: docs/README.md (index with map), 01_thesis_design.md, 02_overview.md, 03_protocol.md, 04_decisions.md (D1–D10: departures from the proposal), 05_results.md, weekly/ (one page per meeting; first: 2026-W45), research/README.md (literature notes). Breadcrumbs and next / previous links on every page; main README, ml_dataset_prep/README.md and models_run/README.md linked into the hierarchy.
  • HTML site: docs/build_site.py (standard library) writes docs/site/*.html from the markdown: sidebar by hierarchy, page contents, Mermaid diagrams, working links between pages.
  • Fixed: Ouassanouan et al. (2026) reference completed (title, DOI, from the proposal); leftover of the chips rename in ml_dataset_prep/README.md ("land use, chip and irrigation method" -> "crop").
  • .gitignore: *.pt and the final models in experiment results.
  • Fixed tile-store path: ml_dataset_prep/03/04 write to outputs/dataset/03_tiles_128px/, but the readers still used 03_tiles/ -> updated in models_run/01, 02a-02d, 03, 03b, tools/a3, a4, a5, docstrings and READMEs (24 places). Without it every models_run script stopped with "views_info.json not found".
  • Checked: config override and typo stop (03); run_experiment.py on E01 (finished runs skipped, compare + report rerun, same numbers); a QUICK_TEST run of the baseline in experiment mode with the PASTIS rotation on the real data (5 rounds, 1.4 min); site: 19 pages, 26 Mermaid diagrams, no console errors, no broken page or section links; all markdown links and anchors resolve.

docs.title: 2026-11-05 (US parcel data: geodatabases converted to shapefiles; IrrMap code checked)
docs.text:
• Data in IrrMap/US_Parcel_Data (outside this repo). New script there: gdb_to_shp.py (settings at top, resumable in chunks). Output next to each source in <gdb name>_shp/, original CRS, checked against the source (same feature count and total area for every layer).
  • Arizona folder = USGS Verified irrigated agricultural lands 2002-17: 14 state layers (AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, ID, IL, MS, MT, NM, TX, UT, WA, WY), irrigated only (IRG_STATUS, IRG_SYS, CROP_TYPE, DATA_DATE, DATA_YEAR).
  • Washington = WSDA crop distribution 2025, 222,520 fields; crop names joined from the WSDACrop table. 137,185 fields have Irrigation = "None" -> candidate rainfed/dryland class (to verify: fallow, pasture, CRP).
  • Colorado CRDSS Div 5 (2000-2023) and Utah WRLU (2017-2024) were already shapefiles.
  • Field names shortened to 10 characters (e.g. InitialSurveyDate -> InitSurvey); dates stored as text YYYY-MM-DD.

  • IrrMap code check: random 80/20 split of single-date patches; ~100% of test patch locations also appear in train on other dates (WA 2018: 31,056 of 31,064) -> their scores are not spatially independent. Test set also used for per-epoch evaluation. Minor bugs (missing argparse import, undefined src_path, constant LAND_TYPE band). Reusable for phase 2: the label sources only, not their patches.

  • Usefulness check (both classes needed):

  • Washington WSDA 2025 - most useful. Field crops (cereal, oilseed, vegetable, hay, seed): 53,723 rainfed (Irrigation = None) vs 33,172 irrigated; rainfed mainly in the dry east (Whitman, Spokane, Lincoln, Adams). Use eastern WA only (semi-arid, winter rain, dryland wheat next to irrigated fields = closest US match to Morocco).
  • Utah WRLU 2017-2025 - useful, adds years. 2023: 15,611 "Dry Crop" vs 110,907 irrigated (fallow/pasture removed). Yearly maps -> temporal transfer test.
  • USGS verified irrigated lands 2002-17 (Arizona folder) and Colorado CRDSS Div 5: irrigated only -> no rainfed class; at most extra irrigated examples.
  • Label definitions: Utah metadata defines "Dry Crop" = no irrigation method applied, crop watered by natural processes (rain); "None" there = non-agricultural land. WSDA has no public definition of Irrigation = "None" (WSDA's own "Dryland Crops" layer = crops grown without irrigation water). 34,235 of the 53,723 WA "None" crop fields come from NASS (CDL), not WSDA ground survey -> irrigation probably not observed. Use DataSource = WSDA only: 19,390 rainfed vs 23,705 irrigated.

docs.title: 2026-11-04 (future phase: US data for spatial and temporal transfer — decision deferred)
docs.text: Discussed after reading IrrMap (Mandal et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.08273). Decision: complete Morocco first; come back to this later. - IrrMap itself is not usable as the study area. It labels irrigation method (flood / sprinkler / drip, all else "other"); there is no rainfed class, so irrigated vs rainfed cannot be studied with it. Its labels come from state agency maps (not field survey); inputs are single-season 224 px patches; validation is a random 80/20 split per state, with no validation split and no spatial test; only a U-Net (ResNet-34) is benchmarked, no GeoFMs. -> Keep Morocco as the AOI (field-surveyed labels, data-scarce region, 12-month time series, spatial folds). Cite IrrMap as related work and as a model for the dataset paper (Part 1). - Idea for a second phase: use the original field boundaries and labels behind IrrMap (state datasets), build chips from scratch with the same pipeline (labels -> 20 km block folds -> tile store -> chips -> embeddings -> same classifiers and validation), to test spatial and temporal transferability. - Why it is valuable: state data often covers many years over the same fields -> clean temporal transfer (train earlier years, test later years), which Morocco cannot offer (year and region overlap); a second continent tests whether GeoFMs transfer better than S1/S2 features (Morocco <-> US). - Conditions: (1) the source data must contain non-irrigated / dryland parcels (deal-breaker; e.g. Washington agricultural land-use data includes dryland wheat — to be checked state by state); (2) small scope: 1-2 states, 3-4 years, ~10-20k parcels; (3) only after Morocco is finished. - Pipeline changes needed: new label reader in ml_dataset_prep/01_prepare_labels.py; support other UTM zones in 03_build_tiles.py (now fixed to UTM 29N; western US spans zones 10-13); US season window via START_MONTH; optional fold by year in 02; a new transfer evaluation (train region/year A, test B). models_run/ unchanged. - Risks: administrative (noisier) labels; different crop systems (Morocco <-> US transfer may be poor for all models); ~4-8 extra weeks. - First step when resuming: one-day check of which state sources IrrMap used, whether they include dryland / non-irrigated fields, which years, and whether field boundaries are downloadable. - Fallback if the check fails: keep as future work; use GMIA-NEXT ground-truth points (tools/a1) or Tunisia as the external test.

docs.title: 2026-11-04 (validation design: PASTIS scheme)
docs.text:
• models_run/03_train_evaluate.py: new setting VALIDATION = "pastis" (default). Per round: 3 folds train, the next fold (k + 1) is the validation fold that chooses the hyperparameters, fold k is the test fold; the model is trained on the 3 training folds. Same scheme as PASTIS (Garnot & Landrieu 2021) and 03b_train_psetae.py, so classifiers and the neural-network baseline are trained, tuned and tested identically. VALIDATION = "nested" keeps the earlier design (inner spatial CV on 4 folds, refit on 4) for a sensitivity check; its runs get the suffix _nested, so run names of the default stay the ones 04_compare_models.py expects.
  • READMEs (main, ml_dataset_prep §5.4, models_run §6.3 + workflow diagram) updated with the rotation table.

docs.title: Progress report
docs.text:
Where the research stands against the research plan and the research proposal: what is finished, what came out, what is next and what is still open. Every individual change is in the change log.

Last updated: 20 November 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The study classifies the 10 m pixels of the surveyed parcels as irrigated or rainfed, so that the trained model can later map the whole cropland area (D16); the earlier parcel-wise experiments are archived. Both study areas are ready: Morocco (2023/24 and 2024/25) and Utah (2023/24), with labelled parcels, five spatial folds and tiles of 12 monthly Sentinel-2 composites.

The experiments were redesigned on 20 November 2026 (D19): two classes (irrigated, rainfed) on the surveyed parcels only, no cropland mask and no weak "not cropland" class; where cropland is becomes a question of the mapping phase (candidate masks: the union of four products, Dynamic World). All earlier 3-class results were removed. E01–E05 are ready and tested and run again, Morocco first (473,675 pixels of 8,775 parcels), then Utah. Wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 composites for the maps are being downloaded from STAC.

docs.title: Research plan
docs.text: The study is organised in five phases that follow the objectives and research questions of the Introduction, followed by a closing phase of synthesis and dissemination.

docs.title: Additions to the proposal structure
docs.text:
The following components are not separate phases in the proposal but are required by the research questions; they are assigned to a phase here.

Component Why it is needed Phase Pixel-wise classification Parcel polygons do not exist for wall-to-wall maps, so every model classifies 10 m pixels; this replaced the parcel benchmark and the separate mapping head of D11 (D16) 2 Second study area RQ4 requires reference labels outside Morocco; Utah (WRLU) became the second, independent study area (D13) 1 Year-transfer test Region and survey year are partly confounded in Morocco; RQ3 is tested in Utah, trained on 2023/24 and applied to 2020/21 (D13) 3 Wall-to-wall imagery the maps need composites of every cropland tile, downloaded from a STAC catalogue (s2_download/) 1, 5 Cropland mask for the maps the experiments classify the surveyed parcels only (irrigated or rainfed), so the cropland extent of the maps and the handling of land that is not cropland are decided in the mapping phase (union of products vs Dynamic World, Cropland extent and mask) 5 Map accuracy and area assessment Map-based area totals are biased without an accuracy assessment against independent reference data 5 Synthesis and dissemination Comparative evaluation, writing and the public release of dataset, code and maps 6

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Results of the pixel-wise experiments, each with its principal finding and main figure. The list of all experiments is on the Experiments page, all runs side by side on the comparison page; the archived parcel-wise results are here.

Experiments redesigned (20 November 2026)

The experiments now classify the pixels of the surveyed parcels into two classes, irrigated and rainfed; the cropland mask and the not-cropland class are left to the mapping phase (D19). All earlier pixel-wise results (three classes) were removed, and E01–E05 run again, Morocco first, then Utah.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page specifies the software environment, the required input data and model weights, the execution order of the scripts and the structure of the repository.

docs.title: 1. Environment
docs.text:
# creates "condaml" (or: conda env update -n condaml -f environment.yml)
conda env create -f environment.yml                 
conda activate condaml

# Clay (--no-deps: avoids an einops conflict with TerraTorch)
pip install --no-deps git+https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model.git  

# AgriFM
pip install mmengine

A GPU (CUDA or Apple Silicon) is recommended for the tile models (experiments E02–E05). Everything else runs on a CPU.

docs.title: 2. Earth Engine
docs.text: Earth Engine is used by pixelwise_run/03_build_tiles.py (tile store), cropland_extent/make_cropland_mask.py (cropland mask), cropland_extent/download_dynamic_world.py (annual Dynamic World layer) and the earlier wall-to-wall route pixelwise_run/06_build_cropland_tiles.py. Put the service-account key in secrets/ (path set at the top of each script), or run earthengine authenticate once. The STAC download s2_download/ needs no account: it reads the public Earth Search catalogue.

docs.title: 3. Input data
docs.text:
File Source Where Field survey, Morocco (parcels with land use and irrigation method) Ouassanouan et al. (2026), Scientific Data data/Morocco_field_survey/lulc_fielddata.shp Water-Related Land Use (WRLU), Utah, one layer per year Utah Division of Water Resources data/Utah_field_data/ Country and state boundaries FAO GAUL 2015 (Morocco), 2024 (Utah) data/admin_boundaries/

The imagery is not downloaded by hand. 03_build_tiles.py fetches the Sentinel-1/2 tile store from Earth Engine; s2_download/02_download_s2_stac.py builds the wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 composites from the Earth Search STAC catalogue (s2_download/README.md).

docs.title: 4. Model weights
docs.text:
All weights are stored in checkpoints/<model>/ and are downloaded automatically on the first run of each experiment that uses the model; later runs reuse them. Folders and sources per model: Foundation models · Weights.

Only the Clay code needs installing by hand (pip install --no-deps git+https://github.com/Clay-foundation/model.git, see Environment above); TerraTorch (Prithvi, TerraMind) and mmengine (AgriFM) come with environment.yml. Presto and TESSERA need no package: their code is cloned into external/presto and external/tessera on first use.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
Run every script from the project folder. Each script has its settings at the top. A description at the top of each script explains what it does and what it writes.

Two pipelines, each in its own folder with the scripts numbered in run order: pixelwise_run/ (current) and parcelwise_run/ (archive); steps 01–03 are the same scripts in both. A third component, s2_download/, downloads the wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 composites from STAC for every cropland tile (training, experiments and maps of the STAC-based approach).

# Pixel-wise pipeline (pixelwise_run/; step table in pixelwise_run/README.md)
python pixelwise_run/01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py      # 01 labels (01_prepare_labels_Utah.py for Utah)
python pixelwise_run/02_make_spatial_folds.py          # 02 spatial folds
python pixelwise_run/03_build_tiles.py                 # 03 tile store (Earth Engine)
python pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py          # 04 labelled pixels, irrigated / rainfed (04_pixel_samples/<season>/)
python experiments/E01_s2_pixel_baseline/run.py        # experiments, one at a time: E01, E02, E03, E04, E05
python pixelwise_run/05_compare_experiments.py         # 05 comparison table and paired tests

# Cropland extent for the mapping phase (cropland_extent/; not used by the steps above)
python cropland_extent/make_cropland_mask.py           # cropland mask per region and year (union of 4 products)
python cropland_extent/download_dynamic_world.py       # annual Dynamic World layer per year (candidate mask)
python pixelwise_run/06_build_cropland_tiles.py        # 06 earlier Earth Engine route for wall-to-wall tiles

# STAC download (s2_download/; details in s2_download/README.md)
EXPERIMENT_REGION=utah python s2_download/01_s2_grid_overview.py      # blocks and Sentinel-2 tiles over the cropland
EXPERIMENT_REGION=utah python s2_download/02_download_s2_stac.py      # monthly composites, every tile with ≥ 1% cropland

On the cluster each run is a Slurm job (jobs/step_cpu.sbatch / jobs/step_gpu.sbatch with SCRIPT=<script>; commands on each experiment page; the STAC download runs as s2_download/s2_dl.sbatch). EXPERIMENT_QUICK_TEST=1 checks a whole experiment on a small subset first. The archived parcel-wise pipeline (parcelwise_run/, steps 01–09; experiments in experiments/parcel_wise_classification/) is described in parcelwise_run/README.md and the Archive.

docs.title: Archive
docs.text:
Finished work that is no longer the current approach. The pages, figures, result tables and scripts are kept unchanged, so every archived result can still be read, checked and re-run.

Archive Period What it is Pages Code and results Parcel-wise classification (E01–E05) Sep – Nov 2026 RQ1 on one label per parcel: frozen GeoFM embeddings (or Sentinel-2 features) averaged inside each parcel, then PCA or L-TAE and a classifier; PSE-TAE from scratch as the neural baseline. Morocco and Utah 2023/24. Results · Experiment plan · Workflow · Models pipeline · Evaluation protocol · Experiments experiments/parcel_wise_classification/

docs.title: Why the parcel-wise experiments were archived
docs.text:
The aim is an annual, continuous (wall-to-wall) map of irrigated and rainfed cropland. A parcel-wise model needs a parcel boundary for every field it classifies, and boundaries exist only for the surveyed parcels. The experiments therefore move to pixel-wise classification: every 10 m pixel gets its own prediction, so the model can be applied to the whole area (pixel-wise experiments).

The parcel-wise results remain the RQ1 evidence for which inputs separate irrigated from rainfed parcels:

  • Morocco: a tie at about 0.91 macro-F1 (PSE-TAE 0.911, S2 + MLP 0.908, Clay + L-TAE 0.906).
  • Utah 2023/24: Clay ahead by about 0.03 (Clay + SVM 0.791 vs S2 + RF 0.764).
  • The classifier and the temporal aggregation change little once the classifier is non-linear; AgriFM is weakest.

docs.title: Re-running an archived experiment
docs.text:
The experiment scripts of the archive (experiments/parcel_wise_classification/) start the parcel-wise training scripts in parcelwise_run/, which write into the archive's results/ folders.

# experiments/parcel_wise_classification/run_experiment.py:  EXPERIMENT = "E02_frozen_pca"
python experiments/parcel_wise_classification/run_experiment.py
# on the cluster
python experiments/parcel_wise_classification/submit_slurm.py

docs.title: Parcel-wise classification · experiments
docs.text:
Archive: parcel-wise classification

Part of the archived parcel-wise experiments (one label per parcel, Sep – Nov 2026). The current experiments classify every pixel: see Experiments. About the archive: Archive.

Every reported result is produced by an experiment: a self-contained folder that records the research question, the complete configuration and the outputs. Each experiment can be re-run from its configuration file and reproduces the reported result.

docs.title: Experiment list
docs.text:
ID Experiment Research question (RQ) Status Headline result (macro-F1) Report E01 Frozen GeoFMs + PCA + classical classifiers (nested spatial CV) RQ1 ✅ done best Clay v1.5 + SVM 0.910; best baseline SVM 0.906; 0 of 16 pairs better, 2 worse than the baseline (Holm) report E02 Frozen GeoFMs + PCA + classical classifiers RQ1 ✅ done Morocco: best Clay v1.5 + SVM 0.901; best baseline SVM 0.900; 0 of 12 pairs better, 2 worse than the baseline (Holm) · Utah 2023/24: best Clay v1.5 + SVM 0.791; best baseline RF 0.764; 4 of 12 pairs better, 2 worse than the baseline (Holm) report E03 Frozen GeoFMs + PCA + MLP head RQ1 ✅ done Morocco: best S2 baseline (MLP) + MLP 0.908; best baseline MLP 0.908; 0 of 4 pairs better, 1 worse than the baseline (Holm) · Utah 2023/24: best TerraMind (MLP) + MLP 0.785; best baseline MLP 0.739; 3 of 4 pairs better, 0 worse than the baseline (Holm) report E04 Frozen GeoFMs + L-TAE temporal aggregation + MLP head RQ1 ✅ done Morocco: best Clay v1.5 (L-TAE) + L-TAE 0.906; best baseline L-TAE 0.905; 0 of 3 pairs better, 0 worse than the baseline (Holm) · Utah 2023/24: best Clay v1.5 (L-TAE) + L-TAE 0.784; best baseline L-TAE 0.743; 2 of 3 pairs better, 0 worse than the baseline (Holm) report E05 PSE-TAE trained from scratch on Sentinel-2 pixel sets (neural baseline) RQ1 ✅ done Morocco: best PSE-TAE + PSE-TAE 0.911; 0 of 1 pairs better, 0 worse than the baseline (Holm) · Utah 2023/24: best PSE-TAE + PSE-TAE 0.755; 0 of 1 pairs better, 0 worse than the baseline (Holm) report

The experiments of RQ1 follow the RQ1 experiment plan: E02 (PCA + LogReg / RF / SVM), E03 (PCA + MLP), E04 (L-TAE + MLP) and E05 (PSE-TAE from scratch), each in Morocco and Utah. Every experiment E02–E05 also includes the label-efficiency runs (10, 25 and 50% of the training blocks), so its report shows a learning curve next to the main result. Ablations A1–A5 are short runs that change one setting of these experiments; their results appear in the report of the experiment they belong to.

The table is refreshed by make_report.py. Status: 📝 planned → 🟦 ready to run → ⏳ running → ✅ done (⏸ parked = kept for a later phase).

docs.title: Where the files of an experiment live
docs.text:
An experiment has two halves: what is run lives in experiments/, what is read lives here in the documentation.

experiments/E02_frozen_pca/          (run)
├── config.yaml        ALL settings of the experiment (the only file you edit to change a run)
└── results/           written by the scripts
    ├── run_info.json      config, code version (git commit), start and end time of every run
    ├── morocco/           one folder per region
    │   ├── <run>/             one folder per input (and per label-efficiency fraction and draw: <run>_f010_d1)
    │   ├── comparison/        all inputs on the same parcels, differences vs the baseline, learning curves
    │   └── breakdown/         results by zone, season and purity (E02)
    └── utah/
experiments/E02_frozen_pca/results_quick/   quick checks (QUICK_TEST), same layout, never used for reports

docs/experiments/E02_frozen_pca/     (read: this website)
├── index.md           setup: question, why, what changes vs the previous experiment, how to run
├── report.md          answer first, then tables and figures (generated) and interpretation (by hand)
└── figures/           figures of the report (written by make_report.py)

experiments/run_experiment.py   runs one experiment from its config: training, comparison, report
experiments/make_report.py      writes tables + figures into report.md, this page, the results page and the menu
experiments/_template/          config.yaml, index.md and report.md to start a new experiment

docs.title: How an experiment runs
docs.text:
flowchart LR CFG["<b>config.yaml</b><br/>inputs · steps · settings"] --> RUN["<b>run_experiment.py</b>"] RUN --> S1["<b>train_evaluate</b><br/>parcelwise_run/03 · once per input"] RUN --> S2["<b>ltae</b><br/>parcelwise_run/03c · once per input"] S1 --> R["results/<region>/<run>/<br/>out-of-fold predictions"] S2 --> R R --> C["<b>compare</b><br/>parcelwise_run/04<br/>same parcels · paired bootstrap"] C --> REP["<b>report</b><br/>make_report.py"] REP --> MD["docs/experiments/<name>/report.md<br/>experiment list · results page<br/>site menu"] EMB[("outputs/morocco/study/02_embeddings<br/>shared by all experiments")] -.-> S1 EMB -.-> S2
  • The scripts in parcelwise_run/ are not edited for an experiment. Each has its settings at the top; in experiment mode the values in config.yaml replace them (same names). A misspelt setting stops the run with an error, so a config can never be silently ignored.
  • Embeddings are shared. They depend only on the dataset and the model, so parcelwise_run/06a–06d are run once and every experiment reads outputs/morocco/study/02_embeddings/.
  • Runs that are finished are skipped, so an interrupted experiment continues where it stopped. RERUN = True (or deleting results/) repeats it.
  • results/run_info.json keeps the config, the git commit and the dates of every run, so a result can always be traced back to the code that produced it.

docs.title: Two pipelines for the monthly embeddings
docs.text:
The foundation models produce one embedding per month (Clay, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind) or one per agricultural year (AgriFM). The two pipelines differ only in how the monthly embeddings are aggregated; all preceding and subsequent steps are shared.

flowchart LR E["Monthly embeddings<br/>12 × D per parcel"] --> P1["<b>PCA pipeline</b> (E01, E02)<br/>concat 12 months → standardise → PCA 128"] E --> P2["<b>L-TAE pipeline</b> (E04)<br/>attention over the 12 months (trained)"] P1 --> K["LogReg · RF · HGB · SVM"] P2 --> H["MLP head"] K --> O["out-of-fold predictions<br/>same format"] H --> O O --> CMP["08_compare_models<br/>same parcels, same bootstrap draws"]

Because both pipelines write the same oof_predictions.csv, the comparison and the report need no change. E04 also lists the E02 runs under compare: EXTRA_RUNS, so PCA and L-TAE are compared on the same parcels and the same bootstrap draws. Details: evaluation protocol §5.

docs.title: Start a new experiment
docs.text:
1. Copy experiments/_template/config.yaml to experiments/E<NN>_<short_name>/config.yaml (next free number; the name says what varies) and experiments/_template/README.md to docs/experiments/E<NN>_<short_name>/index.md.
  2. Edit config.yaml: title, short title (menu), question, changes_from, inputs, steps and only the settings that differ from the script defaults.
  3. Write the setup page index.md: question, why, what changes (a small table against the experiment it builds on).
  4. Set EXPERIMENT = "E<NN>_<short_name>" in run_experiment.py and run it. Use QUICK_TEST: true first to check that everything runs, then set it back to false and delete results/. The report page and the menu entry are created automatically.
  5. When it has finished: write the Answer, Key findings, Interpretation, Caveats and Next steps in report.md (the tables and figures are already there), set status: done and a one-line answer: in the config, run make_report.py once more, and add an entry to the progress log.

A new pipeline variant (another model or aggregation) gets its own script in parcelwise_run/ with settings at the top, the experiment-mode block, and the output format of 07_train_evaluate.py; then add it to SCRIPTS in run_experiment.py.

docs.title: Evaluation protocol, parcel-wise (archived)
docs.text:
Archived: parcel-wise set-up

This page describes the parcel-wise benchmark, now in the archive. The current pixel-wise work: Phase 2 · Model evaluation, evaluation protocol (D16).

This protocol defines the rules common to all experiments and ensures that results are comparable across inputs, classifiers and experiments. Any deviation must be declared in the experiment's What changes table.

Contents: 1 Task · 2 Splits · 3 Inputs · 4 Classifiers · 5 Temporal aggregation · 6 Fairness rules · 7 Metrics · 8 Reading a result · 9 Reporting · References

docs.title: 1. Task and unit
docs.text: The task is binary classification of parcels into irrigated (class 1) and rainfed (class 2), with one label and one prediction per surveyed parcel; all metrics are computed at parcel level. 8,781 parcels (7,585 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed); inputs are scored on the parcels present in every run (8,775: six parcels fully covered by overlapping polygons have no own pixel).

docs.title: 2. Spatial splits
docs.text:
Parcels are grouped into 20 km blocks, and the blocks into 5 folds with the same class balance (about 1,530 irrigated and 240 rainfed parcels each). A block is never split. A place surveyed in both seasons stays in one fold. Block size and fold assignment: dataset §5.

Main design: PASTIS rotation (Garnot & Landrieu 2021). Five rounds; in each, 3 folds train, the next fold is the validation fold, one fold is the test fold:

Round Train Validation (choose settings / early stopping) Test 1 2, 3, 4 1 0 2 3, 4, 0 2 1 3 4, 0, 1 3 2 4 0, 1, 2 4 3 5 1, 2, 3 0 4

The model is trained on the 3 training folds with the setting that scored best on the validation fold. The test fold is never used for any choice. After 5 rounds every parcel has one out-of-fold prediction from a model that never saw its block. Classifiers and neural networks use the same rotation.

Why a rotation rather than one fixed split. (i) Every parcel is tested once, so the rainfed scores rest on all 1,196 rainfed parcels instead of the ~240 of a single test fold. (ii) Five different test areas reveal how strongly accuracy depends on the region, which a single test area would show only by chance. (iii) Hyperparameters are never chosen on the test fold, so the reported accuracy is not inflated by tuning (Varma & Simon, 2006). The same principle of spatially separated folds is implemented in blockCV (Valavi et al., 2019) and used for crop-type classification with Sentinel-1/2 by Orynbaikyzy et al. (2022); Schratz et al. (2019) recommend spatial folds for tuning as well as for testing.

Sensitivity design: nested spatial CV (VALIDATION: nested, experiment E01): settings chosen by spatial CV on the 4 non-test folds, model refit on all 4.

Random CV (stratified, ignoring blocks) is only used inside a run to show how much it overstates accuracy.

docs.title: 3. Inputs
docs.text: Five inputs are compared, all Sentinel-2 only (D14): a Sentinel-2 parcel-feature baseline (12 Sentinel-2 bands, NDVI, NDWI, EVI over 12 months; 180 features) and the embeddings of four frozen foundation models (Clay v1.5, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind, AgriFM). A parcel's embedding is the mean of the patch embeddings that cover it, weighted by the share of each patch inside the parcel; chips are 64 × 64 px and shifted so that the parcel centroid lies at a patch centre. Bands, patch size and temporal handling per model: Foundation models · Configuration.

docs.title: 4. Classifiers
docs.text:
Classifier Grid (chosen on the validation fold, by macro-F1) Fixed logreg logistic regression (linear probe) C ∈ balanced classes, standardised rf random forest max_features ∈ {√p, 0.3} · min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 5} · class_weight ∈ {none, balanced_subsample} 500 trees svm RBF support vector machine C ∈ {1, 10} · γ ∈ {scale, 0.01} balanced classes, standardised

Headline classifiers: random forest (the proposal's baseline classifier) for every input, and logistic regression (linear probe) for the foundation models. SVM is always reported. Histogram gradient boosting was used in E01 and is dropped from E02 on (D6). A trainable MLP head is added in E03 and E04 (parcel-wise experiment plan).

docs.title: 5. Temporal aggregation: two pipelines
docs.text:
How the 12 monthly embeddings of a parcel become one input for the classifier is the step that differs between the two pipelines. Everything before (embeddings) and after (comparison, metrics) is shared.

flowchart LR E["<b>Monthly embeddings</b><br/>12 × D per parcel<br/>(AgriFM: 1 × D)"] --> A["<b>PCA pipeline</b><br/>fill empty months (training median)<br/>→ concat 12 months → standardise<br/>→ PCA 128, fitted on the training folds"] E --> B["<b>L-TAE pipeline</b><br/>standardise per channel<br/>→ L-TAE attention over the months<br/>(empty months masked)"] A --> C["LogReg · RF · SVM (E02)<br/>or MLP (E03)"] B --> D["MLP head, trained with the L-TAE<br/>early stopping on the validation fold<br/>3 seeds"] C --> O["<b>oof_predictions.csv</b><br/>same format"] D --> O O --> CMP["compare: same parcels,<br/>same bootstrap draws"] PCA pipeline L-TAE pipeline Experiments E01, E02, E03 E04 Learns which months matter no (PCA is unsupervised) yes (attention weights) Keeps the order of the months only as positions in the vector yes (positional encoding) Classifier the three of §4 (E02) or an MLP (E03) its own MLP head Applies to the baseline yes (180 features, no PCA) yes (15 variables × 12 months) Applies to AgriFM yes no (one vector per year) Reference linear probing of frozen features PANGAEA: single-date encoders + L-TAE (Marsocci et al. 2024); L-TAE (Garnot & Landrieu 2020)

The L-TAE pipeline is also trained on the monthly Sentinel-2 features, so that the baseline benefits from the same temporal model and the comparison remains balanced. Because both pipelines write the same out-of-fold predictions, E04 compares them directly with the E02 runs on the same parcels.

docs.title: 6. Fairness rules
docs.text:
flowchart LR subgraph SAME["Identical for every input"] P1["same parcels<br/>(common to all runs)"] P2["same pixels<br/>(one tile store)"] P3["same folds<br/>and rotation"] P4["same classifiers<br/>and grids"] P5["same metrics and<br/>bootstrap draws"] end SAME --> D["only the input<br/>(or the one setting the<br/>experiment varies) differs"] D --> C["paired difference<br/>with 95% CI"]
  1. Every fitted step (imputation, standardisation, PCA, tuning, early stopping) uses the training folds only; the validation fold only chooses settings; the test fold is used once, for the prediction.
  2. All inputs come from the same tile store: same composites, cloud mask, months and parcels.
  3. Settings are chosen with the same budget for every input (the grids above).
  4. Inputs are compared on the parcels common to all runs, with the same bootstrap draws.
  5. An experiment varies one thing against the experiment it builds on, and says so in its README.

docs.title: 7. Metrics and uncertainty
docs.text:
Metric Role Macro-F1 headline: mean of irrigated F1 and rainfed F1, so the 14% rainfed class counts equally F1, precision, recall per class rainfed recall: how many rainfed fields are found Balanced accuracy mean recall of both classes Overall accuracy for comparison with the literature (predicting "all irrigated" already gives 86%) PR-AUC (rainfed), Brier score, ECE ranking quality and calibration of the predicted probabilities Macro-F1 per fold, mean ± SD stability across regions (the proposal's selection criterion)

The kappa coefficient is not reported, as it is uninformative for accuracy assessment (Pontius & Millones, 2011).

95% confidence intervals: block bootstrap (Künsch, 1989). The 91 blocks, not the parcels, are the independent units. Each of 1,000 draws resamples whole blocks with replacement and recomputes the metric; the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles give the interval. The same 1,000 draws are used for every run, so a difference between two inputs is measured on identical resamples (paired).

docs.title: 8. How a result is read
docs.text:
• Δ macro-F1 = input − baseline, with the same classifier (runs with their own model, such as L-TAE or PSE-TAE, against the baseline random forest).
  • An input is better (or worse) than the baseline only if the 95% CI of Δ excludes 0 and the Holm-adjusted p-value is below 0.05. Holm corrects for testing all inputs × classifiers together.
  • A CI that excludes 0 without surviving Holm is reported as "higher / lower, not significant after Holm".
  • Otherwise: no clear difference. With ~240 rainfed parcels per fold, differences below about 0.02 macro-F1 are usually inside the noise.

docs.title: 9. Reporting standard
docs.text: Every experiment has a report page (docs/experiments/<name>/report.md) with, in this order: the answer in one or two sentences, the key findings, the setup, the result tables and figures (generated by experiments/make_report.py from the results), the interpretation, the caveats and the next steps. A finished experiment adds a one-line answer to its config.yaml, which appears on the Results page.

docs.title: Parcel-wise experiment plan (archived)
docs.text:
Archived: parcel-wise plan (experiments E01–E05)

This plan describes the parcel-wise experiments, now in the Archive. The current experiments classify pixels: see the pixel-wise experiment plan (D16).

This page is the complete plan of the frozen-encoder evaluation of Phase 2 · Model evaluation (RQ1): which experiments are run, what each one answers, and every setting. It is agreed before the runs start; an experiment page in Experiments is created from it when the experiment is implemented. Rules shared by all experiments (splits, metrics, fairness) are in the evaluation protocol.

Contents: 1 Decisions · 2 Shared settings · 3 Inputs · 4 Design · 5 Main experiments · 6 Label efficiency · 7 Ablations · 8 Analyses · 9 Results pages · 10 Order of work · 11 Size · 12 Open points

Experiment pages (setup, settings, how to run; the report is added when the results are in):

ID Experiment Answers Page E02 PCA + LogReg / RF / SVM Q1 (main table of RQ1) E02 setup E03 PCA + MLP head Q2 · does the head matter? E03 setup E04 L-TAE + MLP head Q3 · does attention over the months help? E04 setup E05 PSE-TAE from scratch Q4 · is a model trained from scratch enough? E05 setup E01 PCA + classifiers, nested CV (done, before D14) check of the validation design E01 setup · report

Label efficiency (Q5) is part of every experiment E02–E05: each one also trains on 10, 25 and 50% of the training blocks (§6). All experiments: Experiments overview.

docs.title: 1. Decisions this plan rests on
docs.text: Decision Choice Reason Input data Sentinel-2 only for every foundation model and every baseline same optical data for all; Morocco and Utah treated alike; Sentinel-1 coverage of Utah changed between years (D14). Sentinel-1 is an ablation for later (A5). Model inputs each foundation model receives only the bands it was pretrained on; no fusion designed by us the comparison tests the pretrained models, not a fusion scheme Classifier heads three classical classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, SVM) and one neural head (MLP) linear probe = standard test of frozen features; RF = standard remote-sensing classifier; SVM = strongest in E01; MLP = trainable head as in GeoFM benchmarks. Gradient boosting is dropped: in E01 it was never the best and always within the CI of SVM (D6). Temporal handling PCA (concatenated months) and L-TAE (learned attention over the months) D8; L-TAE as in PANGAEA (Marsocci et al. 2024) Neural baseline from scratch PSE-TAE on the parcel pixel sets built for parcel classification from satellite time series (Garnot et al. 2020) Most important extra label efficiency the main claim for foundation models is that they need fewer labels Regions Morocco and Utah 2023/24, same protocol, analysed separately D13: two independent study areas

docs.title: 2. Settings shared by every experiment
docs.text: Setting Value Task irrigated (1) vs rainfed (2), one prediction per parcel Morocco data views views/ (2023/24 + 2024/25 pooled), 8,775 parcels scored (7,579 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed) Utah data views views_2023-24/ (WRLU 2024 labels), 6,011 parcels with pixels Time 12 monthly composites of the agricultural year (Morocco Sep–Aug, Utah Oct–Sep) Splits 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; PASTIS rotation: per round 3 folds train, the next fold validates (settings, early stopping), 1 fold tests Tuning grids below, chosen on the validation fold by macro-F1; same grid for every input Fitted steps imputation, standardisation, PCA, tuning and early stopping use the training folds only Neural networks 3 seeds (42, 1042, 2042) per run; mean ± SD over seeds; the out-of-fold prediction of a parcel is the mean probability of the 3 seeds Metrics macro-F1 (headline), F1 / precision / recall per class, balanced and overall accuracy, PR-AUC (rainfed), Brier, ECE Uncertainty block bootstrap, 1,000 draws, same draws for every run; paired differences; Holm over all comparisons of an experiment Comparison set parcels present in every run of the region

docs.title: 3. Inputs
docs.text:
All five inputs are cut from the same tile store. Sentinel-2 only.

Input Data per parcel Bands Patch Per parcel Months Script S2 baseline median of the parcel's inner pixels 12 S2 bands + NDVI, NDWI, EVI (15 variables) parcel 15 × 12 = 180 features 12 03 (view A) Clay v1.5 64 px chip, p8 grid 10 S2 bands 8 px (80 m) 12 × 1,024 12 02a Prithvi-EO-2.0 64 px chip, p16 grid 6 S2 bands (HLS set) 16 px (160 m) 12 × 1,024 12 02b TerraMind 64 px chip, p16 grid 12 S2 bands 16 px (160 m) 12 × 768 12 02c AgriFM 64 px chip, p16 grid 10 S2 bands 4 px patch, stride 32 px (320 m) 1 × 1,024 (whole year) 1 02d Pixel sets (PSE-TAE only) all inner pixels of the parcel 10 S2 bands pixel N pixels × 12 × 10 12 03b (view B)

Patch embeddings are pooled over the parcel with the patch-share weights (models pipeline §5). Clay and Prithvi also receive the parcel location and the date, as in their pretraining; A4 tests whether the location acts as a shortcut.

docs.title: 4. Design: what is varied
docs.text:
Three things are varied: the input, the temporal handling and the head. Not every combination exists: L-TAE is a neural network trained with its own loss, so it cannot feed a random forest, and AgriFM gives one vector per year, so it has no months for L-TAE.

flowchart LR IN["<b>Input</b><br/>S2 baseline · Clay · Prithvi<br/>TerraMind · AgriFM"] --> PCA["<b>PCA</b><br/>12 months concatenated<br/>→ PCA 128"] IN --> LT["<b>L-TAE</b><br/>attention over<br/>the 12 months"] PCA --> CL["<b>Classical</b><br/>LogReg · RF · SVM"] PCA --> MLP1["<b>MLP</b>"] LT --> MLP2["<b>MLP</b><br/>(trained with L-TAE)"] PX["<b>Pixel sets</b><br/>S2, from scratch"] --> PS["<b>PSE-TAE</b>"] CL --> E02(["E02"]) MLP1 --> E03(["E03"]) MLP2 --> E04(["E04"]) PS --> E05(["E05"]) Cell Temporal handling Head S2 baseline Clay Prithvi TerraMind AgriFM Experiment a PCA LogReg · RF · SVM ✓ (no PCA) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ E02 b PCA MLP ✓ (no PCA) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ E03 c L-TAE MLP ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ – E04 d from scratch PSE-TAE pixel sets – – – – E05

Which comparison answers which question

Question Comparison Same in both Q1 · Do frozen foundation-model embeddings beat Sentinel-2 features? each GeoFM vs the S2 baseline, within E02, E03 and E04 head, temporal handling, parcels Q2 · Does the head matter? E02 vs E03 (classical vs MLP) input, PCA Q3 · Does learning which months matter help? E03 vs E04 (PCA vs L-TAE) input, MLP head Q4 · Is a model trained from scratch on our labels enough? E05 vs the best GeoFM setting and the best baseline setting parcels, folds Q5 · Do foundation models need fewer labels? learning curves inside E02–E05 (10 / 25 / 50 / 100% of the training blocks) everything except the training size Q6 · Do the conclusions hold in a second region? every question in Morocco and in Utah protocol

The S2 baseline in E04 (L-TAE on the 15 monthly variables) is the key control for Q1: if L-TAE helps the GeoFMs, the same L-TAE must be given to the raw features, otherwise the gain could come from L-TAE rather than from the embeddings.

docs.title: E02 · PCA + classical classifiers
docs.text:
Setup page: E02

Question Q1 with the classical heads; the main table of RQ1 Inputs S2 baseline, Clay, Prithvi, TerraMind, AgriFM Temporal handling months with no clear pixel filled with the training-fold median → 12 months concatenated → standardised → PCA 128 (fitted on the training folds). AgriFM: 1 × 1,024 → PCA 128. Baseline: 180 features, gaps filled by linear interpolation in time per parcel, standardised, no PCA. Classifiers and grids logreg C ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}, balanced classes · rf 500 trees, max_features ∈ {√p, 0.3}, min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 5}, class_weight ∈ {none, balanced_subsample} · svm RBF, C ∈ {1, 10}, γ ∈ {scale, 0.01}, balanced classes Headline logistic regression (linear probe) for the GeoFMs; random forest for the baseline, as in the protocol; all three reported Runs 5 inputs × 2 regions = 10 runs (3 classifiers each) Script parcelwise_run/07_train_evaluate.py

docs.title: E03 · PCA + MLP
docs.text:
Setup page: E03

Question Q2: does a trainable neural head get more out of the same PCA input than the classical heads? Inputs the same 128 PCA components (baseline: the 180 standardised features) as E02 Head MLP 128 → 256 → 128 → 2, ReLU, batch normalisation, dropout 0.2 (same hidden sizes as the E04 head) Training AdamW, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, class-weighted cross-entropy, up to 100 epochs, early stopping on validation macro-F1 (patience 15), 3 seeds Tuning none beyond early stopping (same budget for every input) Runs 5 inputs × 2 regions × 3 seeds Script parcelwise_run/07c_train_ltae.py, HEAD: mlp on the PCA input

docs.title: E04 · L-TAE + MLP
docs.text:
Setup page: E04

Question Q3: does attention over the months classify better than concatenation + PCA? Inputs monthly sequences: S2 baseline (12 × 15 variables), Clay (12 × 1,024), Prithvi (12 × 1,024), TerraMind (12 × 768). AgriFM excluded (one vector per year). Pre-processing per-channel standardisation with training-fold statistics; months without a clear pixel are masked in the attention, not filled Model L-TAE (Garnot & Landrieu 2020) with the paper's default size: 16 heads, d_k 8, d_model 256, output MLP 256-128; then a linear layer with 2 outputs; sinusoidal encoding of each month's mid-month day (days since the start of the agricultural year), as in L-TAE Training as E03 (AdamW 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, class-weighted cross-entropy, ≤ 100 epochs, patience 15, 3 seeds) Runs 4 inputs × 2 regions × 3 seeds Script parcelwise_run/07c_train_ltae.py, HEAD: ltae Compared with the E03 run of the same input (same head, PCA instead of L-TAE) and the E02 runs

docs.title: E05 · PSE-TAE from scratch
docs.text:
Setup page: E05

Question Q4: does a temporal deep model trained only on our labelled parcels match the frozen foundation models? Input pixel sets: inner pixels of the parcel (edge pixels within 10 m left out; parcels with < 4 inner pixels keep all), 10 S2 bands × 12 months Model PSE-TAE (Garnot et al. 2020): 64 pixels sampled per parcel and month; at prediction the mean of 5 random pixel draws Training Adam 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, ≤ 100 epochs, early stopping on validation macro-F1 (patience 15), 3 seeds Runs morocco_s2, utah_s2 × 3 seeds Script parcelwise_run/07b_train_psetae.py (N_SEEDS = 3)

docs.title: 6. Label efficiency (inside E02–E05)
docs.text:
Label efficiency is not a separate experiment: every experiment E02–E05 also trains each input on fewer training blocks, and its report shows the learning curve next to the main result. The block draws are shared, so the curves of all experiments are directly comparable.

Question Q5: how much training data does each input and head need? Foundation models are expected to gain most when labels are few; the heads with many trained parameters (MLP, L-TAE, PSE-TAE) may lose most. Training size 10, 25 and 50% of the training blocks of each round; 100% = the main run. Validation and test folds stay complete, so only the amount of training data changes. Sampling whole blocks: rainfed and irrigated-only blocks each put in a random order (per region, round and draw), and a fraction takes the first blocks of each list, so the draws are nested (10% ⊂ 25% ⊂ 50%); the order is accepted only if its first 10% hold ≥ 20 rainfed parcels. No fraction below 10%. (In Morocco most rainfed parcels lie in a few Doukkala blocks.) Repeats 3 draws per fraction; draw k is the same in every experiment, for every input and head (paired) Seeds neural runs (E03–E05): 1 seed per draw (the draws give the spread); the main runs keep 3 seeds, and their 100% point on the curve is scored seed by seed, so every point is single-seed Settings label_efficiency block in each experiment's config.yaml; TRAIN_FRACTION and FRACTION_DRAW in scripts 03, 03b and 03c (one shared block-drawing function) Runs per region: E02 45, E03 45, E04 36, E05 9 = 135; 270 for both regions Result in each report: macro-F1 and rainfed F1 vs training fraction, one line per input; in the RQ1 synthesis: all experiments together, the fraction at which each GeoFM reaches the full-data score of the baseline, and whether the best head or PCA vs L-TAE changes with fewer labels Caveat tuning and early stopping still use the complete validation fold, slightly optimistic for a real low-label situation

docs.title: 7. Ablations
docs.text:
Short, targeted runs; each changes one setting of a main experiment.

ID Question Change On Priority A1 Does the yearly profile matter at all? average of the 12 monthly embeddings instead of concat + PCA (FEATURE_MODE: mean) E02, linear probe + SVM high (cheap) A2 Is the PCA size a fragile choice? PCA 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 E02, linear probe medium A3 How many months are needed? 1 peak month / 4 seasonal months / 12 months best setting of each input optional A4 Do Clay and Prithvi use the location as a shortcut? location input switched off (Prithvi USE_COORDS = False, Clay location set to zero); re-embedding needed E02, Morocco (rainfed parcels concentrated in Doukkala) high A5 Does Sentinel-1 add information? TerraMind with Sentinel-1 (terramind-s1s2), baseline with radar features (S1S2_VARIABLES: all), PSE-TAE morocco_s2s1 E02, E04, E05, Morocco only later

E01 (nested spatial CV, done before D14 with Sentinel-1 in the baseline and in TerraMind) stays as the check of the validation design.

docs.title: 8. Analyses on every run
docs.text:
From the out-of-fold predictions; no new training.

Analysis Why Script Paired differences vs the baseline, Holm-adjusted main test of Q1 08_compare_models.py Results by zone, season, parcel size and patch purity region shortcut (Morocco rainfed in Doukkala); small parcels inside 160 m patches 09_breakdown_oof.py Results by crop group (Utah: rainfed alfalfa vs grain) where each input fails later: 09_breakdown_oof.py extension (needs the crop names joined from 01_labels) Random vs spatial CV how much random CV overstates accuracy 07_train_evaluate.py Calibration (Brier, ECE) usable probabilities for maps 03, 03b, 03c Month importance (permutation, L-TAE attention) which part of the season separates the classes 03, 03c Compute cost: parameters, embedding time, training time practical value collected by hand from the run logs

docs.title: 9. Results pages
docs.text:
Every experiment gets its own pages in Experiments, created when it is implemented and filled after each run:

  • index.md (setup): question, what changes against the previous experiment, all settings, how to run.
  • report.md (results): the answer in one or two sentences first, then the generated tables and figures, then the interpretation, caveats and next steps (protocol §9).

Tables and figures are written by experiments/make_report.py from the results, so a page always matches its run. With two regions, every table and figure appears once for Morocco and once for Utah.

Experiment Tables Figures every experiment metrics with 95% CI per input × head; macro-F1 per training fraction (label efficiency); differences vs the baseline (Δ macro-F1, CI, Holm) ; per-fold macro-F1 macro-F1 with CI per input; learning curve (10–100% of the training blocks); macro-F1 per test fold; confusion matrices E02 · PCA + classical the three classifiers side by side; results by zone (focus zone, irrigated-only zones) month importance (permutation, random forest) per input; breakdown by zone and parcel area E03 · PCA + MLP MLP vs the E02 classifiers on the same input; macro-F1 per seed training curves (validation macro-F1 per epoch) E04 · L-TAE + MLP L-TAE vs PCA (E03) on the same input; macro-F1 per seed attention weight per month and class; training curves E05 · PSE-TAE PSE-TAE vs the E02 baseline and GeoFMs; macro-F1 per seed training curves Ablations each ablation vs the setting it changes one comparison figure each

The Results page collects the one-line answer of every experiment; the RQ1 synthesis (step 6 below) compares the experiments and the two regions.

docs.title: 10. Order of work
docs.text:
One experiment at a time: implement, check on a small run, run in both regions, write the report, then the next.

docs.text:
Experiment Runs per region Both regions Hardware E02 5 (× 3 classifiers) 10 CPU, minutes each E03 5 × 3 seeds 30 CPU or GPU, minutes E04 4 × 3 seeds 24 GPU E05 1 × 3 seeds 6 GPU Label efficiency (inside E02–E05) 135 270 CPU (E02) + GPU (E03–E05) Ablations A1, A2, A4 ~15 ~25 CPU (+ GPU for A4 embeddings)

The label-efficiency runs are the largest part; they reuse the code of E02–E05 and only add the training-block subsampling.

docs.title: 12. Open points
docs.text:
• Headline classifier: the protocol keeps random forest for the baseline and the linear probe for the GeoFMs; with SVM the strongest classifier in E01, all three are always reported.
  • Prithvi-EO-2.0 is pretrained on 30 m HLS and applied to 10 m Sentinel-2 (stated as a limitation).
  • Fine-tuning (LoRA, RQ2), the 2024 → 2021 temporal test in Utah (RQ3) and the mapping models follow after RQ1.
