docs.title: 3.1 The field survey
docs.text:
Ouassanouan, Y., Elfarkh, J., Grich, S., Liblab, A., & Chehbouni, A. (2026). Crop and irrigation types ground-truth dataset for Moroccan agricultural regions. Scientific Data, 13, 746. doi:10.1038/s41597-026-06993-y · paper summary

About 10,000 geolocated parcels were surveyed with the QField mobile app between December 2023 and January 2025, in the five main agricultural regions of Morocco. Each record has the land use, crop (45 types), irrigation method (six systems, from flood irrigation to pivots) and a geo-referenced photograph. The authors checked the records against 2024 NDVI time series.

Region Irrigation and crops Survey seasons used here El Gharb surface-water irrigation; rice, vegetables 2023/24 Tadla large-scale irrigation; sugar beet, cereals 2023/24 Doukkala mixed irrigated and rainfed systems (most rainfed parcels) 2023/24 and 2024/25 El Haouz groundwater irrigation; olives, citrus 2023/24 and 2024/25 Souss advanced drip systems; export crops 2024/25

The figures below show the raw survey, before script 01 cleans it. That is why the counts are slightly higher than the 8,781 labelled parcels (e.g. 1,216 rainfed raw vs 1,196 after cleaning; the cleaned parcels are mapped in Figure 1.3). "Statte" is a small survey zone in the 2024/25 season.

Figure 1.1. Surveyed parcels by irrigation method (raw survey). Figure 1.2. Irrigated and rainfed parcels per survey zone (raw survey). Rainfed parcels are almost all in Doukkala, with a few in Souss.

docs.title: 3.2 Other inputs
docs.text: Data Used for Sentinel-2 L2A harmonised + Cloud Score+ monthly imagery of every model (script 03, cloud mask cs_cdf ≥ 0.60) Sentinel-1 GRD monthly VV/VH in the tile store, ascending and descending kept apart; not used by the models for now (D14) FAO GAUL 2015 (level 0) country outline on the maps (data/admin_boundaries/)

docs.title: 4. Script 01 — prepare_labels
docs.text:
Purpose: turn the raw survey into one clean file of labelled cropland parcels. Every later step starts from this file.

flowchart LR A["Survey shapefile"] --> B["Clean geometry<br/>drop empty · repair invalid<br/>drop exact duplicates"] B --> C["Normalise irrigation text<br/>(lower case, trimmed)"] C --> D{"Irrigation<br/>method?"} D -->|"drip · flood · sprinkler<br/>basin · pivot"| E["label 1<br/>irrigated"] D -->|"rainfed"| F["label 2<br/>rainfed"] D -->|"missing"| X["dropped"] E --> G{"Land use is<br/>cropland?"} F --> G G -->|"Seasonal Crop · Trees<br/>Trees + Seasonal"| H["Add attributes<br/>area_ha · ag_season<br/>nn_dist_m"] G -->|"bare soil · weeds · water"| X H --> I["parcels_labelled.geojson<br/>summary.csv · figures"]

Steps

  1. Read the survey shapefile.
  2. Clean the geometry: drop parcels without geometry, repair invalid polygons, drop exact duplicates.
  3. Label it: any irrigation method (drip, flood, sprinkler, basin, pivot) = 1 irrigated; "rainfed" = 2 rainfed. Spelling variants are normalised.
  4. Keep cropland only: Seasonal Crop, Trees, Trees + Seasonal.
  5. Add these attributes:
  6. area_ha: area in UTM 29N.
  7. ag_season: agricultural year of the survey date (1 Sep – 31 Aug, e.g. 2023/24). This decides which imagery a parcel gets.
  8. nn_dist_m: distance to the nearest other parcel.

No cropland mask is used: every surveyed parcel is cropland. The cropland mask serves the mapping phase only (Cropland extent and mask). 6. Save the parcels, a summary table and four figures.

Result

Agricultural year Irrigated Rainfed Total 2023/24 6,189 (11,034 ha) 698 (836 ha) 6,887 2024/25 1,396 (2,020 ha) 498 (1,286 ha) 1,894 All 7,585 1,196 8,781

Median parcel size: 0.83 ha (10th–90th percentile: 0.30–3.5 ha). Rainfed parcels are 14% of the total, and nearly all of them (1,122 of 1,196) are in Doukkala. The classes are unbalanced, and the class is partly tied to the region, which is why section 5 matters.

Figure 1.3. Spatial distribution of the 8,781 labelled cropland parcels. Rainfed parcels are concentrated in Doukkala on the Atlantic coast. Figure 1.4. Class balance (left; 86.4% irrigated, 13.6% rainfed) and parcel-size distribution per class (right, logarithmic axis). Figure 1.5. Labelled parcels by survey month (December 2023 – January 2025). The survey date determines the agricultural year, and thus the imagery, assigned to each parcel.

Outputs (outputs/morocco/dataset/01_labels/): - parcels_labelled.geojson - summary.csv - parcels_map.png - class_balance_and_size.png - survey_timing.png

docs.title: 5. Script 02 — make_spatial_folds
docs.text: Purpose: split the parcels into 5 folds so a model can be trained on some areas and tested on other areas. This is the dataset's train / validation / test split.

docs.title: 5.1 Why not a random split
docs.text: Surveyed parcels are typically a few hundred metres apart, and neighbouring parcels usually share a class. Under a random 5-fold split, 72% of test parcels have a training parcel within 250 m and 98% within 1 km. Accuracy then reflects the recognition of nearby parcels rather than the ability to map new areas, a bias documented by Roberts et al. (2017), Ploton et al. (2020) and Kattenborn et al. (2022).

docs.title: 5.2 Choosing the block size
docs.text:
The range of spatial dependence is estimated from the proportion of parcel pairs that share a class as a function of their distance. This proportion is compared with the random-placement level, i.e. the probability that two randomly drawn parcels share a class, 0.86² + 0.14² ≈ 76%. Beyond the distance at which the curve reaches this level, proximity carries no information about the class.

Distance between parcels 0.2 km 1 km 5 km 10 km 15 km 20 km 30 km 50 km Same class (%) 96.1 95.2 92.0 91.0 86.7 81.4 79.7 73.7 Figure 1.6. Proportion of parcel pairs sharing a class as a function of distance. The proportion approaches the random-placement level (76%, dashed) at about 20–30 km, which motivates the 20 km block size (dotted).

Candidate block sizes, each with 5 greedy-balanced folds:

Split Rainfed in smallest fold Rainfed share per fold Test parcels with a training parcel ≤ 250 m ≤ 1 km random 239 20–20% 79.4% 98.4% 2 km blocks 239 20–20% 12.8% 65.6% 5 km 239 20–20% 6.3% 31.7% 10 km 239 20–20% 3.2% 18.0% 20 km 238 20–20% 2.0% 10.2% 25 km 239 20–20% 1.8% 9.1% 30 km 142 12–34% 0.6% 4.6% 50 km 202 17–24% 1.2% 5.9%

20 km is the chosen size: - It is near the distance where class similarity approaches the random-placement level. - It cuts leakage to 2% at 250 m. - It still gives five folds with equal class shares.

From 30 km upwards there are too few blocks with rainfed parcels to balance the folds: one fold would hold 12% of the rainfed parcels and another 34%.

docs.title: 5.3 Fold assignment
docs.text:
flowchart TD A["Parcel centroids<br/>(UTM 29N)"] --> B["20 km × 20 km grid<br/>→ 91 occupied blocks"] B --> C["Sort blocks: most rainfed parcels first<br/>(ties in random order, seed 42)"] C --> D["Take next block"] D --> E["Put it in the fold whose larger<br/>class share would stay lowest"] E --> F{"Blocks left?"} F -->|yes| D F -->|no| G["fold 0–4 for every parcel<br/>+ stratified random_fold for comparison"]

Resulting folds (whole blocks per fold):

Fold Irrigated Rainfed Blocks 0 1,528 239 12 1 1,528 239 13 2 1,473 241 42 3 1,528 238 11 4 1,528 239 13

Leakage, all folds averaged:

Training parcel within … 100 m 250 m 500 m 1 km 5 km random split 24.1% 71.7% 90.1% 97.7% 99.7% 20 km spatial split 0.4% 1.8% 3.8% 8.1% 38.0% Figure 1.7. Fold assignment of the parcels (left) and class counts per fold (right). Each fold contains about 1,530 irrigated and 240 rainfed parcels. Figure 1.8. The 20 km blocks and their folds, with enlargements of Doukkala (A) and Tadla (B). Whole blocks are assigned to a single fold. Figure 1.9. Distance from each test parcel to the nearest training parcel under a random split (median 154 m) and under the 20 km spatial split (median 6.8 km).

docs.title: 5.4 How the folds give train, validation and test
docs.text:
There is no single fixed train / validation / test split. The folds take turns, as in the PASTIS benchmark (Garnot & Landrieu 2021): in each of 5 rounds, 3 folds train, the next fold validates (chooses the hyperparameters) and one fold is the test fold.

Round Train Validation Test 1 folds 2, 3, 4 fold 1 fold 0 2 folds 3, 4, 0 fold 2 fold 1 3 folds 4, 0, 1 fold 3 fold 2 4 folds 0, 1, 2 fold 4 fold 3 5 folds 1, 2, 3 fold 0 fold 4

After 5 rounds every parcel has been tested once, by a model that never saw its block. Unlike PASTIS, the folds are made of whole 20 km blocks, so the test fold is always a set of regions the model has never seen.

For quick experiments, the column split gives one fixed split: fold 0 = test, fold 1 = validation, folds 2–4 = train. random_fold gives a stratified random split, so the optimism of random validation can be measured.

Outputs (outputs/morocco/dataset/02_folds/): - parcels_folds.geojson: parcels + block_id, fold, random_fold, split - fold_counts.csv - block_size_comparison.csv - class_similarity_by_distance.csv / .png - leakage_check.csv - spatial_folds.png, spatial_folds_blocks.png - train_test_distance.png

docs.title: 6. Script 03 — build_tiles
docs.text: Purpose: build the single image store that every model reads from.

docs.title: 6.1 Tile grid and which tiles are built
docs.text:
• One projection for the whole area, UTM 29N (EPSG:32629), with 10 m pixels. The few parcels in zone 30N are resampled.
  • A fixed grid of 128 × 128-pixel tiles (1.28 km × 1.28 km). Tile IDs are <season>_<ix>_<iy>, e.g. 2023-24_412_3561.
  • Only the tiles the parcels need are built:
  • home tile: holds the parcel centroid;
  • outline tiles: touched by the parcel polygon;
  • context tiles: reached by the largest model chip around the centroid. That is 64 px plus up to 8 px of alignment shift, i.e. 40 px (400 m) in every direction.
flowchart LR P["Parcel<br/>centroid + outline"] --> H["home tile<br/>(contains centroid)"] P --> O["outline tiles<br/>(polygon crosses into them)"] P --> C["context tiles<br/>(within 32 + 8 px of the centroid)"] H --> U["Union over all parcels<br/>and both seasons"] O --> U C --> U U --> T["Tile plan:<br/>each tile built once"]

docs.title: 6.2 Two agricultural years
docs.text:
The survey ran from December 2023 to January 2025, so the parcels belong to two agricultural years. Each parcel must be described by the imagery of the season in which its label was observed. A field that was irrigated in 2023/24 may be rainfed or fallow in 2024/25. The two years are therefore handled as two separate, parallel tile stores that share one grid:

flowchart TD A["Survey date of each parcel"] --> B["<b>ag_season</b> = agricultural year (1 Sep – 31 Aug)<br/>Sep–Dec of Y → Y/Y+1 · Jan–Aug of Y → Y−1/Y"] B --> P1["<b>2023/24</b> · 6,887 parcels<br/>tile plan: tile_id = 2023-24_ix_iy"] B --> P2["<b>2024/25</b> · 1,894 parcels<br/>tile plan: tile_id = 2024-25_ix_iy"] P1 --> X1["Label rasters: only 2023/24 parcels<br/>Earth Engine image Sep 2023 – Aug 2024<br/>(2023/24 tiles + 2 km)"] P2 --> X2["Label rasters: only 2024/25 parcels<br/>Earth Engine image Sep 2024 – Aug 2025<br/>(2024/25 tiles + 2 km)"] X1 --> T1["2,183 tiles (2023/24)"] X2 --> T2["804 tiles (2024/25)"] T1 --> S["One folder tiles/, one grid (same ix, iy),<br/>season in every tile name"] T2 --> S S --> V["04_make_pixel_samples.py samples each parcel's pixels<br/>from the tiles of its own season"]

How each part of the pipeline handles the season:

Where How the season is handled 01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py ag_season from the survey date: 1 Sep – 31 Aug (a parcel surveyed in Jan 2024 → 2023/24; Dec 2024 → 2024/25) Tile plan a tile is the triple (season, ix, iy). The same 1.28 km square can exist once for each year, with the same grid position. Tile name the season comes first: 2023-24_374_2793, 2024-25_374_2793 Label rasters only parcels of the tile's own year are burnt in, so a 2024/25 parcel never appears as a label in a 2023/24 tile Imagery one 12-month Earth Engine image per year, built over that year's tiles only. The month bands are named identically (m01 … m12), so both years have the same 228-band layout and models can mix them. QA, tiles.parquet one row per (season, tile), with an ag_season column Pixel samples (04_make_pixel_samples.py) one sample set per season (04_pixel_samples/<season>/); each parcel's pixels come from the tiles of its own season. (The archived 04_make_views.py likewise cut every parcel from the tiles of its own season.) Folds (02) blocks are defined by location only, so a place surveyed in both years falls in the same block and fold. No information leaks between years from training to test. Viewing (tools/a4_build_vrt.py) one virtual raster per year, because the two years overlap in space

Currently 47 tile positions exist in both years: places with parcels surveyed in 2023/24 and in 2024/25.

Why the agricultural year (September – August).

gantt dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD axisFormat %b section Rainfed cereals Pre-season :r0, 2023-09-01, 2023-11-01 Sowing :r1, 2023-11-01, 2024-01-01 Growth, flowering Mar–Apr :r2, 2024-01-01, 2024-05-01 Harvest :r3, 2024-05-01, 2024-07-31 section Irrigated land Green whenever water is applied :i1, 2023-09-01, 2024-06-01 Dry summer :crit, i2, 2024-06-01, 2024-08-31 Reason Explanation One complete rainfed cycle rainfed cereals are sown in November–December and harvested in May–July; a calendar year would divide the cycle The dry summer carries the signal from June to August only irrigated fields remain green, the clearest contrast between the classes (confirmed by the permutation importance in E01) Irrigation status is seasonal rainfall, reservoir allocations and fallowing change which fields are irrigated, so a label is valid for one season Consistency with existing products LGRIP30, WorldCereal and GMIA-NEXT define irrigation for one growing season (Teluguntla et al., 2023; Van Tricht et al., 2023; Kebede et al., 2026) National convention the Moroccan agricultural campaign, including the accounting of seasonal rainfall, starts on 1 September

docs.title: 6.3 Monthly composites (per tile, per month)
docs.text:
flowchart TD subgraph S2["Sentinel-2 L2A"] direction TB A1["Scenes with cloud cover < 60 %"] --> A2["Cloud Score+ mask:<br/>keep pixels with cs_cdf ≥ 0.60"] A2 --> A3["Median of clear pixels<br/>12 bands, reflectance × 10,000"] A3 --> A4["+ S2_NCLEAR: number of<br/>clear observations"] end subgraph S1["Sentinel-1 GRD (IW, VV + VH)"] direction TB B1["Split by orbit:<br/>ascending / descending"] --> B2["dB → linear power;<br/>monthly mean"] B2 --> B3["→ dB × 100<br/>VV, VH per orbit"] B3 --> B4["+ S1_N: number of scenes"] end A4 --> M["One month = 19 bands"] B4 --> M M --> Y["12 months (Sep → Aug) = 228 bands, int16<br/>NODATA = −32768 where no observation"]
  • 19 bands per month:
  • B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B8A, B9, B11, B12
  • S2_NCLEAR
  • VV_ASC, VH_ASC, S1_N_ASC
  • VV_DSC, VH_DSC, S1_N_DSC
  • Months: m01 = September … m12 = August of the parcel's agricultural year. Band names in the GeoTIFF look like B4_m03 (red, November).
  • Why linear power for Sentinel-1: backscatter in dB is a logarithm. Averaging in dB gives the geometric mean and biases the composite downwards. Averaging is therefore done in linear power, and the result converted back to dB.
  • Why the orbits are kept apart: ascending and descending passes look at a field from different incidence angles, so their backscatter is not interchangeable. Both are stored; the archived view script picked one. The current models use Sentinel-2 only (D14).
  • Each tile's _scenes.json lists the Sentinel-1/2 scene IDs used in each month, so every pixel can be traced to its source.

docs.title: 6.4 Label rasters (local, no Earth Engine)
docs.text:
Each tile has a 3-band int32 label raster on exactly the same grid:

Band Values Meaning label 0 / 1 / 2 0 = unlabelled or ignore, 1 = irrigated, 2 = rainfed parcel_idx 0 / 1…N 0 = no parcel, otherwise the parcel's row in parcels.csv edge 0 / 1 1 = parcel pixel within 10 m of the outline (mixed boundary pixel)

Rules:

flowchart TD A["Parcel polygon<br/>(same season as the tile)"] --> B{"Contains at least<br/>one pixel centre?"} B -->|yes| C["Burn pixels whose<br/>centre is inside"] B -->|no: very small parcel| D["Burn all touched pixels<br/>flag all_touched = True"] C --> E{"Pixel claimed by<br/>two parcels?"} D --> E E -->|yes| F["label = 0, parcel_idx = 0<br/>(ignore) · pair listed in parcel_overlaps.csv"] E -->|no| G["label, parcel_idx set"] G --> H["edge = 1 if within 10 m<br/>of the outline"]

Only parcels of the tile's own agricultural year are burnt in.

docs.title: 6.5 Steps
docs.text:
1. Read the parcels with folds and project them to UTM 29N.
  2. Parcel table: index, centroid, bounds, area, perimeter, pixel counts (all and inner), home tile, tiles needed.
  3. Tile plan (6.1).
  4. Label rasters for all planned tiles (6.3). Local and fast.
  5. Earth Engine: one 228-band monthly image per agricultural year. Each tile is downloaded with computePixels, 8 requests in parallel and up to 4 retries, and written as a compressed GeoTIFF with its scene IDs. Finished tiles are skipped on a restart.
  6. Tile index (tiles.parquet) with fold, role, labelled pixels and QA.

DOWNLOAD = False stops after step 4, so the plan and labels can be checked without Earth Engine. N_TEST_TILES = 20 builds only 20 tiles per season, for a test run.

docs.title: 6.6 Quality numbers per tile
docs.text:
Column Meaning s2_nodata_pct share of tile-months without any clear Sentinel-2 pixel s2_nodata_parcel_pct the same, on parcel pixels only s2_nclear_parcel_median median number of clear observations on parcel pixels, per month s1_asc_months, s1_dsc_months months with at least one ascending / descending scene role home, outline or context mixed_folds the tile holds parcels from more than one fold (relevant for segmentation, section 11)

Outputs (outputs/morocco/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/): - tiles/<id>_img.tif, tiles/<id>_lab.tif, tiles/<id>_scenes.json - parcels.csv - parcel_overlaps.csv - tiles.parquet - tiles_qa.jsonl - tiles_info.json

docs.title: 6.7 Visual check of tiles — 03b_tile_quicklooks.py
docs.text:
03b_tile_quicklooks.py draws one figure per tile for a visual check of the tile store: the 12 monthly composites as true colour (B4/B3/B2), NDVI and Sentinel-1 VH, the three label rasters (label, parcel index, edge pixels) and the mean NDVI and VH per month of the irrigated and rainfed parcel pixels. By default it selects, per agricultural year, the three downloaded home tiles with the most pixels of both classes, the tile with the most irrigated pixels and the tile with the most rainfed pixels (Sentinel-2 missing data < 1 %); TILE_IDS selects tiles explicitly. The Sentinel-1 orbit with more observations in the tile is drawn (ORBIT = "auto"). The region is set with REGION at the top, as in scripts 02–04.

Output: outputs/<region>/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/quicklooks/<tile_id>.png

docs.title: 7. Script 04 — pixel samples
docs.text:
Purpose: turn the labelled parcels into labelled pixels for the pixel-wise models. The script pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py runs locally and needs no Earth Engine. It reads the label rasters and images of the tile store and writes one table per agricultural year with the 12-month series, label, parcel, fold and position of every sampled pixel. Only pixels of the surveyed parcels are taken (two classes, irrigated and rainfed); no cropland mask is used. Classes, sampling rules, output files and counts are documented on the page Pixel samples.

Season Pixels Irrigated (parcels) Rainfed (parcels) 2023/24 367,882 336,211 (6,183) 31,671 (698) 2024/25 105,793 83,672 (1,396) 22,121 (498) Pooled 473,675 419,883 (7,579) 53,792 (1,196)

Output: outputs/morocco/dataset/04_pixel_samples/<season>/ (pixels_X.npy, pixels.parquet, summary.csv, samples_info.json). The earlier three-class samples with not-cropland pixels are kept in 04c_pixel_samples/ and are no longer used.

docs.title: Archived: model views (parcelwise_run/04_make_views.py)
docs.text:
Archived: parcel-wise set-up

The model views below served the archived parcel-wise classification (parcel features, pixel sets, 64 px chips for parcel embeddings). They are no longer used; see the Archive.

Purpose: cut every model input from the tile store. It runs locally and needs no Earth Engine.

flowchart TD TS["<b>Tile store</b><br/>tiles read through a cache of 48 tiles"] --> L["<b>For each parcel</b><br/>read its window and its pixels<br/>(label raster: parcel_idx = this parcel)"] L --> A["<b>View A · parcel features</b><br/>median per band and month + NDVI, NDWI, EVI<br/>parcel_features_all.csv · parcel_features_inner.csv"] L --> B["<b>View B · pixel sets</b><br/>all parcel pixels, all months<br/>pixelsets.npz"] L --> C["<b>View C · 64 × 64 chips</b><br/>patch-aligned, per patch size<br/>chips_p8/ (Clay) · chips_p16/ (others)"] TS --> D["<b>View D · full tiles</b><br/>as they are, for<br/>segmentation models"]

docs.title: 7.1 View A — parcel feature tables
docs.text:
• Per parcel and month: the median over the parcel's pixels of each of these:
  • the 12 Sentinel-2 bands (reflectance 0–1);
  • NDVI = (B8 − B4)/(B8 + B4);
  • NDWI = (B8 − B11)/(B8 + B11), which measures canopy water;
  • EVI = 2.5 (B8 − B4)/(B8 + 6 B4 − 7.5 B2 + 1);
  • VV and VH for both orbits (dB).
  • Indices are computed per pixel first, then the median is taken.
  • The median is used instead of the mean because it is robust to leftover clouds and mixed edge pixels.
  • Observation counts are added: the mean S2_NCLEAR over the parcel, and the maximum S1_N per orbit.
  • Column names are <variable>_m<month>, e.g. NDVI_m10 (NDVI in June). Each parcel has 19 variables × 12 months = 228 feature columns, plus counts and metadata (parcel_id, label, ag_season, fold, n_px_used, used_inner).
  • parcel_features_inner.csv leaves out edge pixels. A parcel with no inner pixel falls back to all of its pixels (used_inner = False).

docs.title: 7.2 View B — pixel sets
docs.text:
All pixels of each parcel, unaggregated, for set-based temporal models such as PSE-TAE (Garnot et al. 2020).

  • pixels [N_pixels, 12, bands] int16
  • offsets [parcels + 1]: parcel i = pixels[offsets[i]:offsets[i+1]]
  • edge [N_pixels], parcel_id, label, bands

docs.title: 7.3 View C — patch-aligned chips for the foundation models
docs.text:
Vision-transformer foundation models partition an image into square patches: 8 × 8 px for Clay and 16 × 16 px (160 m) for Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind and the output grid of AgriFM. Each patch is represented by one embedding.

When a chip whose size is a multiple of the patch size is centred on the parcel, the centroid falls on the corner of four patches, and a small parcel is distributed over four patches dominated by neighbouring fields. Shifting the chip by half a patch places the centroid at the centre of a single patch:

flowchart LR subgraph OLD["Centred chip (old)"] O1["Centroid on the corner<br/>of 4 patches"] --> O2["Parcel split over 4 patches,<br/>each mostly neighbouring fields"] end subgraph NEW["Patch-aligned chip (now)"] N1["Chip shifted by half a patch<br/>(4 px for p8, 8 px for p16)"] --> N2["Centroid at the centre<br/>of one patch"] N2 --> N3["Higher share of the pooled<br/>patches inside the parcel"] end OLD -.->|"replaced by"| NEW

Purity measures this. A patch's weight is the share of its pixels inside the parcel, and those weights are also what the archived parcel-wise set-up used to pool patch embeddings. Purity is the weighted share of parcel pixels in the pooled patches: Σ w² / Σ w, from 0 to 1. index.csv stores both purity (aligned) and purity_centred (old rule), so the gain is measurable.

Each chip folder holds: - part_*.npz: chips [n, 12, 15, 64, 64] int16, mask [n, 64, 64] (parcel pixels), parcel_id. - index.csv: one row per parcel. Columns: part, label, ag_season, fold, zone, lat, lon, epsg, x0, y0 (chip top-left corner, for georeferencing), area_ha, n_px, n_px_in_chip, purity, purity_centred. - chips_info.json: band order and scales. The 15 bands are B1 … B12, VV, VH, S2_NCLEAR.

Figure 1.10. Patch purity, i.e. the share of the pooled patches that lies inside the parcel, for centred chips (grey) and patch-aligned chips (blue), at 8 px (80 m, left) and 16 px (160 m, right) patch size. Alignment markedly increases purity, in particular for 8 px patches.

docs.title: 7.4 Sentinel-1 orbit for views B and C
docs.text: S1_ORBIT = "auto" picks the orbit direction with more valid tile-months over the whole study area and writes it to views_info.json (s1_orbit_for_chips_and_pixelsets). That orbit's bands are named simply VV and VH in the chips. "ASC" or "DSC" force one orbit. View A keeps both orbits as separate columns.

docs.title: 7.5 QA files
docs.text:
• qa_clear_obs.csv: clear observations per parcel and month.
  • qa_purity.csv: purity distribution per patch size.
  • views_info.json: settings, the chosen orbit, and counts.

docs.title: 7.6 Dataset inspection
docs.text:
The checks of the archived parcelwise_run/05_inspect_dataset.py (archived models pipeline §4) characterise the parcel-wise dataset before any model is trained.

Figure 1.11. Mean number of clear Sentinel-2 observations per parcel and month (left) and share of parcels without any clear observation (right). Winter months have the fewest clear views, yet every parcel has at least one clear observation in every month. Figure 1.12. Monthly parcel medians of NDVI, NDWI and Sentinel-1 VH backscatter (median and interquartile range per class). Irrigated parcels show markedly higher vegetation and moisture signals from December to April and higher backscatter throughout the year; rainfed parcels show a weak, short spring peak. Figure 1.13. Example irrigated parcels: 16 px-aligned chips for the 12 months of the agricultural year, in true colour and NDVI (outline = parcel). Figure 1.14. Example rainfed parcels, displayed as in Figure 1.13.

docs.title: 8. Output layout and file formats
docs.text:
outputs/morocco/dataset/
├── 01_labels/
│   ├── parcels_labelled.geojson         EPSG:4326 polygons
│   └── summary.csv, *.png
├── 02_folds/
│   ├── parcels_folds.geojson            + block_id, fold, random_fold, split
│   └── fold_counts.csv, block_size_comparison.csv, leakage_check.csv, class_similarity_by_distance.csv, *.png
└── 03_tiles_128px/agyear/
    ├── tiles/
    │   ├── <tile_id>_img.tif            int16, 228 bands (12 months × 19), NODATA −32768, EPSG:32629, 10 m
    │   ├── <tile_id>_lab.tif            int32, 3 bands: label, parcel_idx, edge
    │   └── <tile_id>_scenes.json        scene IDs per month (S2, S1 asc, S1 dsc)
    ├── parcels.csv                      one row per parcel (parcel_idx = value in the label raster)
    ├── parcel_overlaps.csv              overlapping parcel pairs, their labels and overlap share
    ├── tiles.parquet                    GeoParquet tile index: geometry, season, role, fold(s), QA
    ├── tiles_info.json                  grid, bands, months, scales, cloud settings
    └── views/                           archived parcel-wise views (parcelwise_run/04_make_views.py)
        ├── parcel_features_all.csv      view A
        ├── parcel_features_inner.csv    view A, edge pixels removed
        ├── pixelsets.npz                view B
        ├── chips_p8/  chips_p16/        view C: part_*.npz, index.csv, chips_info.json
        ├── qa_purity.csv, qa_clear_obs.csv
        └── views_info.json
04_pixel_samples/<season>/               (in outputs/morocco/dataset/) labelled pixels, one folder per year
    ├── pixels_X.npy                     int16 [pixels, 12 months, 19 bands]
    ├── pixels.parquet                   label, parcel, fold, block, zone, tile, position per pixel
    ├── summary.csv                      pixels and parcels per class and fold
    └── samples_info.json                settings, band order, class codes, CRS

Scales: - Sentinel-2: reflectance × 10,000. - Sentinel-1: dB × 100. For example, −1,523 = −15.23 dB. - Counts: plain integers. - −32,768 = no observation. Count bands are 0 there.

docs.title: 9. How to use the dataset
docs.text:
Model family Use Train / validation / test Pixel models: random forest, gradient boosting, TempCNN (E01, E02) pixel samples (04_pixel_samples/<season>/), Sentinel-2 bands fold (5 rounds: 3 train / 1 validation / 1 test) Tile models: frozen foundation models with L-TAE + UPerNet, U-TAE, fine-tuning (E03–E05) full tiles: _img.tif (Sentinel-2 bands) + _lab.tif, loss only on the labelled pixels of the training folds same folds; scored at the labelled pixels of the test fold Annual maps (Phase 5) wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles over the cropland mask (s2_download/) –

Minimal example: read the pixel samples.

import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
folder = "outputs/morocco/dataset/04_pixel_samples/2023-24"
X = np.load(f"{folder}/pixels_X.npy")                  # [pixels, 12, 19] int16
meta = pd.read_parquet(f"{folder}/pixels.parquet")      # label, fold, parcel_id, tile_id, row, col, ...
info = json.load(open(f"{folder}/samples_info.json"))
red_june = X[0, 9, info["month_bands"].index("B4")] / 10000

Archived: parcel-wise set-up

In the parcel-wise set-up, random forest and gradient boosting used view A, pixel-set models (PSE-TAE) view B, and the foundation models view C (chips_p8 or chips_p16 with mask, split by index.csv); see the Archive.

docs.title: 10. Running, settings and run time
docs.text:
conda activate condaml
python pixelwise_run/01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py   # minutes
python pixelwise_run/02_make_spatial_folds.py      # minutes
python pixelwise_run/03_build_tiles.py             # Earth Engine; a few hours; resumable
python pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py      # local; SEASONS per region in the script
# archived parcel-wise step: python parcelwise_run/04_make_views.py

Scripts 02–04 serve both study regions: set REGION = "morocco" at the top of each (the default). The settings that differ between regions (projection, agricultural year, block size, map boundaries) are in pixelwise_run/regions.py; the Utah dataset is built the same way (Utah training data).

Run 03 first with N_TEST_TILES = 20, then check the result with pixelwise_run/03b_tile_quicklooks.py before the full run (the archived parcel-wise checks used parcelwise_run/05_inspect_dataset.py and tools/a3_export_chips_geotiff.py).

To view the whole tile store as one layer, tools/a4_build_vrt.py writes virtual rasters (one per agricultural year: labels, true / false colour and Sentinel-1 per month) to outputs/morocco/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/vrt/. They only point to the tiles, so nothing is copied.

The settings sit at the top of each script:

Script Main settings 01 SEASON_START_MONTH (= 9, from regions.py), CROP_KEEP, IRRIGATED_TEXT, RAINFED_TEXT, CHECK_WORLDCOVER 02 REGION, N_FOLDS = 5, BLOCK_KM (= 20, from regions.py), CANDIDATE_KM, SEED = 42 03 REGION, TILE_PX = 128, GSD_M = 10, CRS_EPSG (= 32629, from regions.py), CHIP_PX = 64, MAX_SHIFT_PX = 8, INNER_BUFFER_M = 10, CLOUD_COVER_PERCENTAGE = 60, CS_THRESHOLD = 0.60, DOWNLOAD, SEASONS = None (all years; or one year at a time), DOWNLOAD_WORKERS = 8, N_TEST_TILES 04 REGION, SEASONS (Morocco: 2023/24 and 2024/25), MAX_PX_PER_PARCEL = 100, NONCROP_PX_PER_TILE = 100, NONCROP_BUFFER_PX = 2, SEED = 42 04 (archived, parcelwise_run/04_make_views.py) REGION, SEASONS = None (all years → views/; one year → views_<year>/), CHIP_PATCH_SIZES = [8, 16], CHIP_PX = 64, S1_ORBIT = "auto", MAKE_FEATURES, MAKE_PIXELSETS

Earth Engine access uses a service-account key in secrets/, which is never committed.

docs.title: 11. Known limitations
docs.text:
• Class balance and geography: 14% of parcels are rainfed, and 94% of those are in Doukkala. A model can partly learn "region" rather than "irrigation". Per-zone results should be reported.
  • Reprojection: the few parcels in UTM 30N are resampled to 29N.
  • Monthly composites: in cloudy winter months some parcels have no clear Sentinel-2 view (NODATA). The counts show where.
  • Tile models (full tiles): a tile can hold parcels of two folds (mixed_folds), and context tiles reach across fold borders. Tile-level models need their own tile split, or a loss mask restricted to the training fold.
  • Labels: a single survey visit per parcel. Overlapping parcels are set to ignore and listed, but labels are not otherwise checked against imagery.

docs.title: Phase 1 · Data preparation
docs.text: Phase 1 provides the data on which all later phases rely: labelled reference parcels, a spatial partition for validation, a common store of monthly imagery from which every model input is derived, the labelled pixels of the pixel-wise models and, for the mapping phase, the cropland products, the cropland mask and the wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles. The labels, the pixel samples and the experiments do not use a cropland mask; the mask serves the maps only. Every model uses Sentinel-2 only (D14). The design ensures that differences between models are attributable to the models rather than to their input data.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component Content Status Page 1a · Morocco training data 8,781 labelled cropland parcels (7,585 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed); 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; 2,987 tiles of 128 × 128 px with 12 monthly composites × 19 bands (2023/24 and 2024/25) ✅ complete Morocco training data 1b · Utah training data (second study area, D13) 12,015 WRLU crop fields in 550 sampled cells: WRLU 2024 (5,000 irrigated, 1,013 rainfed) and WRLU 2021 for the temporal test (4,987 irrigated, 1,015 rainfed); 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; tile plan of 5,436 tiles ✅ 2023/24 labels, folds and tiles complete; pixel samples to be rebuilt with the two-class script; 2020/21 labels, folds and label rasters prepared for the temporal test Utah training data 1d · Cropland extent and mask for the mapping phase only: union of 4 cropland products per region and agricultural year (D17); Morocco 103,068 km², Utah 9,979 km² of cropland (2023/24); annual Dynamic World layer as an alternative (download_dynamic_world.py); the mask is chosen in Phase 5 ✅ union: Morocco 2023/24 and 2024/25, Utah 2023/24 and 2020/21; 📝 Dynamic World Cropland extent and mask 1e · Pixel samples (input of every experiment) labelled pixels of the surveyed parcels, two classes (irrigated, rainfed), with folds (04_pixel_samples/); Morocco 2023/24 (367,882) and 2024/25 (105,793): 473,675 pixels of 8,775 parcels in 2,015 tiles ✅ Morocco 2023/24 and 2024/25; ⏳ Utah 2023/24 to be rebuilt with the two-class script; Utah 2020/21 to be built for the temporal test Pixel samples 1f · Wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles (STAC) 12 monthly Sentinel-2 composites for every 128 px tile with ≥ 1% cropland, from the Earth Search STAC catalogue (s2_download/); Utah 18,472 and Morocco 112,536 tiles (2023/24) 🔄 Utah 2023/24: 17,278 of 18,472 tiles, the rest to be rerun after a bug fix; Morocco on hold Cropland extent and mask §5 1c · Multi-year imagery, Morocco tiles for 2021–2025 for the annual maps 📝 prepared in Phase 5 –

Archived: parcel-wise set-up

The parcel-wise set-up derived three further views from the tile store (parcel feature tables, pixel sets and patch-aligned 64 px chips, parcelwise_run/04_make_views.py). These views are no longer used; see the Archive.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
Step Script Output 01 pixelwise_run/01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py or 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py cleaned, labelled cropland parcels (one script per region, same output layout) 02 pixelwise_run/02_make_spatial_folds.py fold (0–4) per parcel 03 pixelwise_run/03_build_tiles.py tile store from Google Earth Engine 04 pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py labelled pixels (irrigated, rainfed) of the surveyed parcels for the pixel-wise models (04_pixel_samples/<season>/) M1 cropland_extent/make_cropland_mask.py cropland mask per region and agricultural year (union of 4 products; mapping phase only) M2 cropland_extent/download_dynamic_world.py annual Dynamic World layer per agricultural year (most frequent class, mean crop probability, image count); candidate mask for the maps 06 pixelwise_run/06_build_cropland_tiles.py wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles over the cropland mask from Earth Engine (earlier route for the mapping stage) S01 s2_download/01_s2_grid_overview.py download blocks of 10.24 km over the cropland tiles, the Sentinel-2 tiles over them, overview figures S02 s2_download/02_download_s2_stac.py (cluster wrapper s2_dl.sbatch) monthly Sentinel-2 composites (SCL cloud mask, monthly median) of every tile with ≥ 1% cropland, from the Earth Search STAC catalogue (sentinel-2-c1-l2a)

The archived parcel-wise pipeline (parcelwise_run/) uses the same steps 01–03, then 04_make_views.py (parcel features and chips) and the parcel model scripts 05–09 (Archive).

Steps 02–06 serve both regions: set REGION = "morocco" or "utah" at the top (the STAC download reads the region from the environment variable EXPERIMENT_REGION). The settings that differ per region (projection, agricultural year, block size, map boundaries) are in pixelwise_run/regions.py. All outputs of a region are in outputs/<region>/ (dataset/, cropland_extent/, s2_download/, study/ and, for Morocco, analysis/). The STAC download is documented in s2_download/README.md; its tiles follow the grid and tile_id of the cropland mask and serve training, experiments and maps of the STAC-based approach.

The scripts, design choices, figures and output formats are documented in Morocco training data and Utah training data. The data providers are listed in Data sources; departures from the proposal are recorded as decisions D1, D2, D4, D9, D13, D14, D16 and D17.

docs.title: Reuse in later phases
docs.text: The scripts are region- and period-independent: the Utah dataset (1b) is produced with the same scripts 02–04, and the multi-year imagery (1c) by changing the agricultural years.

docs.title: Pixel samples for pixel-wise classification
docs.text:
The continuous maps classify every 10 m pixel on its own, so the models are trained and tested on pixels, not on parcels (D16). pixelwise_run/04_make_pixel_samples.py turns the labelled parcels into labelled pixels. It creates no new labels: the label of a pixel is the survey label of its parcel, which 03_build_tiles.py already wrote into the label raster of each tile. The script picks pixels and writes one row per pixel: its 12-month time series, its label, parcel, fold and position. Every pixel-wise experiment starts from this table, so all models see the same pixels.

One tile in Doukkala (2023/24, 15 surveyed parcels): (1) Sentinel-2 tile with the surveyed parcels; (2) label raster of 03: one label per parcel on all its pixels, edge pixels marked and skipped; (3) inner pixels and the sampled pixels: at most 100 per parcel, so the 6 larger parcels are cut to 100; (4) every sampled pixel takes its parcel's fold and 20 km block (all parcels of this tile lie in one block, so one fold); (5) NDVI of the sampled pixels per class; (6) the output table, one row per pixel.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
Code Class Pixels taken from 1 Irrigated inner pixels of irrigated parcels 2 Rainfed inner pixels of rainfed parcels

All surveyed parcels are cropland, so the experiments compare models on the irrigated / rainfed decision alone (D19). No cropland mask is used to select pixels. Pixels outside the surveyed parcels are not used: their class is unknown. Where cropland lies, and how land that is not cropland is handled, is decided in the mapping phase (Cropland extent and mask, Phase 5).

docs.title: Sampling rules
docs.text:
• Inner pixels only. Pixels within 10 m of a parcel outline (edge band of the label raster) mix the field with its neighbours and are skipped; a parcel without any inner pixel falls back to all its pixels (edge_fallback).
  • At most 100 pixels per parcel, drawn at random (seed 42), so a few large irrigated fields do not dominate and the pixels of one parcel stay a small group.
  • Folds. Every pixel takes its parcel's fold and 20 km block of the spatial folds, so a parcel is never split between training and test.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
outputs/<region>/dataset/04_pixel_samples/<season>/

File Content pixels_X.npy int16 [pixels, 12 months, 19 bands]: the bands of the tile store (12 Sentinel-2 bands, clear-observation count, Sentinel-1 VV / VH and scene counts per orbit), NODATA −32768; the experiments use the Sentinel-2 bands only (D14) pixels.parquet one row per pixel, same order: label, class_name, parcel_idx, parcel_id, fold, block_id, zone, tile_id, row, col, x, y (UTM pixel centre), lon, lat, edge, edge_fallback summary.csv pixels and parcels per class and fold samples_info.json settings, band order, class codes, CRS

The earlier three-class samples (with not-cropland pixels) are kept unchanged in 04c_pixel_samples/; no experiment reads them.

docs.text:
Fold 2023/24 irrigated 2023/24 rainfed 2024/25 irrigated 2024/25 rainfed 0 69,104 4,130 15,559 6,814 1 62,922 6,154 16,616 4,666 2 72,720 10,134 22,557 1,173 3 65,290 8,444 20,426 1,986 4 66,175 2,809 8,514 7,482

Limitations.

  • Rainfed is the minority class (about 1 rainfed pixel per 8 irrigated pixels when the two years are pooled); the models need class weights.
  • The rainfed pixels are unevenly spread over the folds and years (e.g. 1,173 in fold 2 of 2024/25 but 10,134 in fold 2 of 2023/24), so the rainfed scores vary between test folds.

docs.title: Utah training data
docs.text:
This page describes the Utah dataset, the second, independent study area (D13). It is built with the same pipeline as the Morocco training data: only the label script (01_prepare_labels_Utah.py) is region-specific; scripts 02–04 are the same files, run with REGION = "utah". As in Morocco, the experiments classify the labelled 10 m pixels of the crop fields as irrigated or rainfed (D16); no cropland mask is used. The experiments run in Morocco first; Utah follows later with the same plan.

Status

Labels (01), spatial folds (02) and the tile plan with label rasters (03) are complete for WRLU 2024 (2023/24) and WRLU 2021 (2020/21). For 2023/24 the tile images (03) are complete; the pixel samples (04) are to be rebuilt on the cluster with the two-class script (04_pixel_samples/), after which E01–E05 follow the Morocco runs. The earlier three-class samples are kept in 04c_pixel_samples/ and are no longer used. The 2020/21 data are prepared for the temporal test (RQ3). The wall-to-wall Sentinel-2 tiles of the STAC download (s2_download/) are described in Cropland extent and mask §5.
